findings.description: TypeError on Google Meet booking when destinationCalendar is empty — Any Google Meet booking without a destination calendar crashes in `EventManager.create`, because `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration` so the check fails safely.

Office365 createEvent uses first host's destination calendar for every credential — `EventManager` calls `createEvent` once per destination credential, yet it always uses `destinationCalendar[0]`. Other hosts' credentials then write to the wrong calendar, causing errors or duplicates.
Collective hosts' destination calendars dropped when destinationCalendar is null — Assign the combined, de-duplicated array instead of pushing.
Meet link patch uses undefined calendarId when no destination calendar matches — Compute `selectedCalendar` with the `"primary"` fallback once and use it in both the insert and the patch.

updateLocation loses externalCalendarId because updateEvent returns no externalId — `CalendarManager.updateEvent` never returns `externalId`, so `result.externalId` is undefined and references created after a location edit lose `externalCalendarId`, breaking later updates and deletes. Return `externalId` from `updateEvent`, or reuse the existing reference's `externalCalendarId`.

Recurring cancel deletes all remaining events once per calendar reference — The recurring-cancel branch now runs inside the `bookingCalendarReference` loop, so with N references each remaining event gets N delete calls, and the repeats fail or double-delete. Run it once, guarded by a flag or moved outside the loop.

deleteEvent fallback searches destinationCalendar for a falsy externalId, always undefined — The fallback only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, yet it searches `event.destinationCalendar` for that falsy value, so it is always undefined and deletes hit `"primary"`. Use `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId` instead.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:254-256`

goldensDetail.text: When externalCalendarId is absent, updateEvent/deleteEvent look for a destination calendar whose externalId equals that absent value, so the lookup never matches and the configured destination calendar is no longer used.
The organization slug is now set only when team billing is enabled (inverted condition), so with billing both slug and requestedSlug are set and without billing neither is.

Office365 (and Lark) createEvent ignore the new credentialId argument and always use the first destination calendar, so in collective bookings other hosts' credentials target the organizer's calendar instead of their own.

The Google Meet fallback reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining, so a Meet booking with a null or empty destinationCalendar throws instead of falling back to Cal Video.

For collective events whose organizer has no destination calendar, destinationCalendar is null and the optional push drops all other hosts' destination calendars, so those hosts never get calendar events.
Video booking references are now saved without their credentialId, so cancelling the booking can no longer find the video credential and the meeting is not deleted.

Cancelling all remaining occurrences of a recurring collective booking deletes only the first calendar reference of each booking, repeated once per host, so the other hosts' events stay on their calendars.

In Google createEvent, when no destination calendar matches the credentialId, the hangout-link events.patch is called with an undefined calendarId and fails, so the Meet link is not added to the event description.

When cancelling a recurring booking with multiple calendar references, the recurring-event deletion over all remaining bookings and credentials runs once per reference, causing duplicate delete calls and errors.

findings.description: Team admin check uses && so admins who are not owners are denied — Legitimate team admins who are not owners cannot add guests to team bookings they do not host. Combine the `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` checks with `||` instead of `&&`.

Case-sensitive guest email check bypasses blacklist and duplicate attendee check — A mixed-case address like `Blocked@Example.com` slips past `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` and the duplicate attendee check. Compare `guest.toLowerCase()` against the blacklist and the attendee emails.

Calendar update uses caller's credentials instead of the organizer's — `EventManager` is built from `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, so when an attendee or team admin adds guests, the organizer's calendar event fails to update or errors. Build the credentials and `EventManager` from `booking.user`, and catch calendar failures.

sendAddGuestsEmails called with unfiltered guests instead of uniqueGuests — A re-submitted existing attendee is treated as new and gets the 'scheduled' email instead of the 'guests added' one. Pass `uniqueGuests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails` instead of `guests`.

Guests array has no maximum length, enabling email spam and load — Without a limit, any user with booking access can submit a huge `guests` list, creating many attendee rows and flooding recipients with emails. Add `.min(1).max(N)` to the `guests` array with a reasonable N.

Calendar update failure aborts handler after guests are saved, skipping emails — If a calendar integration throws in `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`, the mutation errors and skips emails even though guests are saved, and a retry hits `emails_must_be_unique_valid`. Wrap the call in try/catch and log the error.

Duplicate guest emails in input are not deduplicated on the server — Duplicates within `guests` pass through `uniqueGuests`, so a direct tRPC call can create duplicate attendee rows and emails. Dedupe the input on the server with a lowercased `Set` and compare against existing attendees case-insensitively.

goldensDetail.text: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, so only team owners pass; team admins who are not organizer or attendee are wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN.

The guest blacklist is lowercased but incoming guest emails are compared without normalization, so a blacklisted address submitted with different casing bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and is added and emailed.
The server never deduplicates the guests array, so a request with the same email twice inserts duplicate attendee rows for the booking.

The handler passes the unfiltered guests list to sendAddGuestsEmails, which uses it to pick who gets AttendeeScheduledEmail, so existing attendees included in the request receive a new-booking confirmation instead of the add-guests email.

EventManager is created with the requesting user's credentials, so when a non-organizer adds guests the organizer's calendar event is not updated (or the wrong account is used) for references without a credentialId.
sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings, so hosts and attendees receive add-guests emails even when standard emails are disabled.

The add-guests handler omits booking.iCalUID from the CalendarEvent, so the add-guests emails' .ics attachments use booking.uid as UID and recipients' calendars treat them as a new event rather than an update of the original booking invite.
Guest email uniqueness is checked case-sensitively, so case variants of the same address are accepted as distinct guests (and slip past the lowercased blacklist).

findings.description: Safe-parse result stored as credential key instead of parsed data — Saving the whole safe-parse result makes the stored key `{ success, data }`, so later `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails and the credential breaks. Store `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data` as `key`.

Sync-mode refreshOAuthTokens returns raw Response instead of token data — Callers read `res.data` or `.accessToken`/`.expiresIn`, which are undefined on a `Response`, so Google's TypeError is swallowed and Hubspot computes a NaN expiry. Parse the JSON in `refreshOAuthTokens` and adapt it to each caller's shape, or have callers call `response.json()`.

Credential id passed as userId to refreshOAuthTokens — The sync endpoint receives a credential id as `calcomUserId`, so it refreshes tokens for the wrong user or none. Pass `credential.userId` through `biginAuth` and `refreshAccessToken` instead of `credentialId`.

Salesforce token refresh bypasses refreshOAuthTokens and credential sync — Calling Salesforce directly bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens`, so for synced credentials `parseRefreshTokenResponse` can store the placeholder refresh token, Salesforce rejects it, and no connection is created. Wrap the fetch in `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "salesforce", credential.userId)` and skip the local refresh when synced.

Salesforce connection built with stale access token after refresh — The fresh token is saved, but the `jsforce.Connection` still uses the old `credentialKey.access_token`, so calls can fail with an expired session. Use `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` and its instance URL, and route the refresh through `refreshOAuthTokens`.

Salesforce token refresh and DB write run on every service instantiation — `getClient` runs in the constructor, so every instantiation adds a blocking token refresh and a DB write, risking Salesforce rate limits. Refresh only when the stored token is expired or a call fails with an auth error.

Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time !== operator — Comparing with `!==` leaks timing information, letting an attacker recover the secret and overwrite any user's app credentials. Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers and handle a missing header value explicitly.

goldensDetail.text: The webhook parses the body with zod .parse and decrypts/JSON-parses the keys without error handling, so invalid payloads produce 500 errors instead of 400 responses.
parseRefreshTokenResponse writes the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when the refresh response omits a refresh token, so the stored credential gets an invalid refresh token and later refreshes fail.

minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys from z.string().toString(), which produce a literal key rather than a wildcard, so the sync-mode schema does not validate or keep expiry and other token fields as intended.
Google Calendar persists the safeParse result object instead of its data as the credential key, corrupting the stored credential so later reads fail.
Salesforce getClient now refreshes the OAuth token and writes the credential on every service construction, adding a network round trip and DB write even when the access token is valid.
The new Salesforce token refresh uses prisma without importing it, so the code fails type checking and throws a ReferenceError at runtime.
Salesforce checks response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok when refreshing the token, which can misclassify successful responses, and then ignores the refreshed token.
After refreshing the Salesforce token, jsforce.Connection is created with the stale access_token and instance_url instead of the newly refreshed values.

The app-credential webhook looks up appStoreMetadata by app.slug, but the map is keyed by dirName, so apps whose slug differs from their directory (e.g. google-calendar) always get a 404 and their credentials cannot be synced.

findings.description: SMS cron deletes non-SMS reminders with retryCount > 1 — Because the `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` branch isn't limited to SMS, this cron can delete email or WhatsApp reminders, including already scheduled ones. Move `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` outside the OR, or add it to the `retryCount` branch.

Unguarded retryCount update in catch block can abort the reminder loop — If `prisma.workflowReminder.update` throws in the catch block (row deleted concurrently, DB down), the exception escapes the loop, skips the remaining reminders and makes the cron return an error. Wrap the update in its own try/catch and log the failure.

`retryCount` is not incremented when `message` is empty or `sendTo` is missing — Reminders with an invalid or absent phone number are never counted as failed, so the cron reselects them on every run until `scheduledDate`, which is the retry loop this PR should remove. Add an else branch that increments `retryCount` when `message` or `sendTo` is missing.

goldensDetail.text: retryCount is set to reminder.retryCount + 1 from a value read at the start of the run instead of an atomic increment, so overlapping runs can lose increments.
The deleteMany OR clause applies retryCount > 1 without the SMS method filter, so the SMS cron deletes any workflow reminder (email, WhatsApp) with retryCount above 1.

The retry-count update inside the catch block is not guarded, so if it throws (for example the reminder was deleted concurrently) the error escapes the loop and the cron run fails, skipping the remaining reminders.
Claims transient errors increment retryCount, so two runs during an outage delete the whole pending SMS reminder queue.

SMS-sending locks are counted as failed scheduling attempts: scheduleSMS returns undefined for locked users/teams, retryCount is incremented, and after two cron runs the retryCount > 1 cleanup deletes future reminders even if sending is later unlocked.

findings.description: Backup code login bypasses password check when junk totpCode is supplied — A junk `totpCode` plus a valid `backupCode` skips the password check, so a backup code alone authenticates. Make the password check run whenever `backupCode` is present, for example `if (user.password && (!credentials.totpCode || credentials.backupCode))`.

Backup code consumption is non-atomic and allows concurrent reuse — Two concurrent logins can both find the same code in the decrypted `backupCodes` before either update commits, so a one-time code gets reused. Replace `prisma.user.update` with an `updateMany` conditioned on the original `user.backupCodes`, and throw `IncorrectBackupCode` when no rows change.

Dismissing dialog on backup codes step skips onEnable and state reset — Closing via Esc or overlay click on the `DisplayBackupCodes` step skips `resetState` and `onEnable`, so the parent never learns 2FA was enabled and the modal reopens on that step. Run both in `onOpenChange` for that step, or call `onEnable` right after the enable succeeds.

goldensDetail.text: The credentials authorize() skips the password check when any totpCode is present, and the new backup-code branch never validates that totpCode, so a backup code plus a dummy totpCode logs in without the account password.

findings.description: getBaseConditions returns unwrapped OR fragments, breaking AND precedence — For org and team scope, `authConditions` and `filterConditions` are top-level `A OR B` fragments, so a caller appending `AND <extra predicate>` gets the wrong precedence and returns bookings outside the authorized scope. Wrap the single-branch returns of `getBaseConditions` in parentheses with `Prisma.sql`.

goldensDetail.text: The getBaseConditions test uses a single booking matching both auth and filter conditions, so it would pass even if the conditions were not combined.
The new public options type makes teamId optional for team scope, so a missing teamId compiles and silently yields empty insights instead of a type error.
Claims getBaseConditions returns OR fragments without parentheses, so a caller appending `AND <extra>` would leak rows outside the authorization scope.

findings.description: Raw HTML posts skip sanitization, allowing stored XSS from imported content — Imported feed content such as `<script>` tags or event-handler attributes reaches the forum unsanitized, which makes stored XSS possible. Sanitize `raw` in the `raw_html` branch of `Post#cook`, or before storing it in `TopicEmbed.import`.

Unescaped URL interpolated into raw HTML link allows markup injection — The `url` can contain single quotes or angle brackets, so a crafted feed link can break out of the `href` attribute and inject markup. Escape it with `ERB::Util.html_escape` for both the href and the text, and anchor the check with `\A`.

Embed is created for an unsaved post when PostCreator fails — `PostCreator#create` returns an unsaved post on failure, so `TopicEmbed.create!` raises on a nil `post_id` and aborts the whole `PollFeed` run. Check `post.persisted?` and `creator.errors.blank?` before creating the embed.

Nil content on feed item raises NoMethodError and aborts the poll loop — A feed item with no `content` makes `i.content.scrub` raise `NoMethodError`, which stops the poll and skips all later items. Fall back to `i.description`, skip blank items, and rescue per-item errors.

goldensDetail.text: The referer and embed_url host checks compare against SiteSetting.embeddable_host case-sensitively, so a host differing only in case is rejected even though hostnames are case-insensitive.

PollFeed reads i.content.scrub for every feed item, so items without a content element (common in RSS feeds that only have description) raise NoMethodError and abort the import of the remaining items.

TopicEmbed.import appends a footer that interpolates the URL unescaped into an <a href='...'> tag in raw HTML that is later rendered unsanitized, so a crafted URL can inject markup; it also appends to contents with << without handling nil.
When the embedded post has been deleted, TopicEmbed.import's update path passes a nil embed.post to PostRevisor and crashes on every later import of that URL.
Claims import_remote crashes on unparseable pages (nil content) and dead URLs because it does no nil check or network error handling around open(url).read.

absolutize_urls only handles root-relative paths: protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/x.png are rewritten to http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png and path-relative links are left unresolved, breaking links and images in imported posts.

Every retrieval of an article not yet embedded synchronously polls and imports the entire RSS feed, and since throttling is per URL, many different article requests repeat the full feed download and processing.

The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' specs leave feed_polling_enabled at its false default, so they never reach the condition they name and would pass with those checks deleted.
`import_remote` fetches the embed URL with open-uri, which follows redirects, so the embeddable-host check on the initial URL can be bypassed to reach internal services (SSRF).
The retrieve throttle is keyed by the full embed URL, so an anonymous client can vary the query string on the embeddable host to bypass it and make the server create an unbounded number of topics.

The "requires feed_polling_enabled?" spec leaves feed_polling_url and embed_by_username at their blank defaults, so poll_feed is skipped regardless and the test would pass even without the enabled check.
The embed layout references the 'embed' stylesheet and embed.js, but neither is in config.assets.precompile, so with precompiled assets in production the embed page fails to load them.

findings.description: Migration crashes when embed_category or uncategorized_category_id row is missing — On a default install the `embed_category` row is absent, so `[0]` is nil and the migration raises NoMethodError, blocking the deploy. Fetch `.first` into a variable and fall back to 0 when nil, for both the `embed_category` and `uncategorized_category_id` lookups.

Migration inserts unnormalized embeddable hosts with unescaped raw SQL — The raw INSERT bypasses the model's `before_validation`, so legacy values like `http://discourse.org` are stored with scheme or path and `record_for_host` never matches them, breaking embedding after upgrade. Normalize each value (strip scheme and path, downcase, skip blanks) and quote it before inserting.

before_validation callback raises NoMethodError when host is nil — A request with a missing `host` raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a validation error. Skip the `sub!` calls when `host` is blank, or assign a non-mutating `sub` result, so `validates_format_of` reports the problem.

update and destroy raise NoMethodError (500) for unknown host ids — An unknown or already-deleted id makes `update` and `destroy` dereference nil, returning a 500 instead of a 404. Use `EmbeddableHost.find` or raise `Discourse::NotFound` when nil, and check that the nested `params[:embeddable_host]` exists in `save_host`.

record_for_host fails to downcase host, rejecting registered hosts with uppercase — Registered hosts are rejected when the incoming URL has uppercase characters, because `record_for_host` compares `lower(host)` against a non-downcased `uri.host`. Compare with `host.downcase` instead.

Host validation accepts ports that record_for_host can never match — A host saved with a port can never match, because `record_for_host` compares only `uri.host`, so embedding silently fails for it. Remove the port from the validation regex, or match `host:port` when `uri.port` is non-default.

Host category set from local categoryId instead of server-saved category_id — For a new host with no chosen category, the local `categoryId` is null while the server stores the uncategorized category, so the badge is empty until reload. Set `category` from the `category_id` in the saved response instead of `categoryId`.

goldensDetail.text: The migration reads execute(...)[0]['id'] for embed_category without checking for an empty result, so installs without that setting stored crash the migration instead of falling back to the uncategorized category.

After saving a host, the component overwrites its category with findById(categoryId); when no category was chosen this is null even though the server saved the uncategorized category, so the row shows no category until reload.
Hosts saved with a port (allowed by the validation regex) are stored as host:port, but lookup compares only URI.host, so those configured hosts never match and embedding fails for them.
EmbeddableHost's host format validation only accepts TLDs of 2-5 letters, so admins cannot add embeddable hosts on longer TLDs like example.technology.

The flex-item styles target the inner .extra-info-wrapper instead of the component's root div, so in the flexbox header a long topic title keeps its full width and pushes the navigation panel out instead of being truncated.
The align-items mixin emits no -moz-box-align, so on old Firefox versions using the display:-moz-box fallback the advertised vertical centering is not applied.

Removing the float-based right alignment of .d-header .panel leaves the server-rendered (no-JS) header's login panel, which sits inside .row and is not a flex item, no longer right-aligned next to the title.

Making .small-action a flex container leaves .small-action-desc content-sized (no flex:1), so the right-floated edit/delete buttons inside it sit right after short action descriptions instead of at the right edge of the row.

On mobile the .small-action custom message keeps margin-left:-40px, tuned for the old 4em left padding; with the new flex layout and 1.5% padding it is pulled into the avatar column and overlaps the icon.

findings.description: `downsize` is defined twice, so the second definition replaces the first — `Jobs::ResizeEmoji` still calls `OptimizedImage.downsize` with five arguments, so every emoji resize job now raises `ArgumentError`. Remove the duplicate and update the `Jobs::ResizeEmoji` call to pass "100x100", or keep one method that accepts both forms.

Hard-coded 10MB upload limit overrides max_attachment_size_kb for attachments — The hard-coded 10MB limit ignores `max_attachment_size_kb`, so the browser blocks valid attachments above 10MB and lets oversized ones through below it. Apply the 10MB cap only when `type === 'image'`, keep the site setting for attachments, and fix the 413 handler the same way.

Image downsize loop ignores failures and passes a percentage to gifsicle — With `allow_animation: true`, GIFs go to `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`, which expects WxH, so the command likely fails. `OptimizedImage.downsize` then returns false, the loop ignores it, and oversized GIFs are never shrunk after 5 wasted attempts.

goldensDetail.text: downsize is defined twice in OptimizedImage; the new (from, to, dimensions, opts) version overrides the (max_width, max_height) one, so existing callers such as ResizeEmoji that pass width and height now raise ArgumentError.

The client-side upload size check hardcodes 10 MB instead of the per-type max_<type>_size_kb setting, so attachment limits diverge from the server: larger allowed attachments are blocked and smaller limits are only enforced server-side.
The upload downsizing passes a percentage ('80%') as dimensions, but for animated GIFs the gifsicle path uses --resize-fit, which expects WxH geometry, so downsizing silently fails.
Auto-downsizing passes the upload tempfile path, which lacks a .gif extension, so the animated branch is never chosen and convert keeps only the first frame, flattening oversized animated GIFs.
Claims the downsize loop checking tempfile.size may never terminate because of a stale cached size, causing infinite loops.
Oversized SVG uploads go through the new ImageMagick downsize loop because SVG counts as an image, so the vector file is rasterized or corrupted in place before Upload.create_for parses it as SVG.

The upload tempfile path, which for API URL uploads embeds the request-controlled type param, is now passed to OptimizedImage.downsize and run unescaped in a shell via backticks, allowing command injection through type.
The 413 upload error message states a hard-coded 10 MB maximum that may not match the limit the server or web server actually enforces.

findings.description: Group members page only loads the first 50 members with no paging — `model.findMembers()` runs once with the default limit of 50, and the `group/members.hbs` template has no paging controls, so larger groups silently show only 50 members. Add pagination to the public members view, or request a limit that covers the whole group.

totalPages overcounts by one when user_count is a multiple of limit — When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, `totalPages` counts an extra page, so `showingLast` stays false on the real last page and 'next' loads an empty page. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

Unbounded limit and negative offset in group members endpoint — `limit` comes straight from `params[:limit].to_i`, so a huge value serializes an entire large group in one request and a negative value causes a database error. Clamp `limit` between 1 and 200, and use `[offset, 0].max` for `offset`.

goldensDetail.text: The admin group pager computes total pages as floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so when the member count is an exact multiple of the limit it shows an extra page and Next navigates to an empty member list.
Paging actions fire overlapping member requests and each response unconditionally overwrites offset and members, so a stale response arriving last can revert the list to an earlier page.
The public members endpoint now always caps results at 50 per page, but the public group members page has no pagination, so groups with more than 50 members are silently truncated for users.
Creating a group ignores the alias_level the admin selected, saving only name and visibility, so new groups keep the default alias level.
Removing a member deletes the membership row directly and skips clearing the user's primary_group_id, so a removed user can keep this group as their primary group.
Group member pagination is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit: Next moves to offset == user_count and shows an empty page.
Admin remove_member deletes memberships with group.users.delete, which skips GroupUser callbacks, so the cached groups.user_count is never decremented and stays inflated.

Admin add_members pushes every username into group.users without skipping existing members, so adding someone already in the group hits the unique group_users index, returns a 500 and leaves earlier users partially added.
The public group members endpoint takes `limit` from params with no upper bound or positivity check, letting a visitor request huge pages or trigger a 500 with a negative limit.
Admin remove_member calls group.users.delete with a raw integer id, which raises RecordNotFound (404/500) when the user is not or no longer a member, e.g. on concurrent removal.

findings.description: Fallback locales only loaded from controller, not jobs, mailers or with_locale — Because only `ApplicationController#set_locale` calls `ensure_loaded!`, jobs, mailers, and `I18n.with_locale` blocks like `PostDestroyer` never load fallback files and silently fail to fall back. Load every locale in `I18n.fallbacks[config.locale]` inside `I18n.translate`/`load_locale` instead.

goldensDetail.text: Fallback locale catalogs are only loaded in the controller's set_locale filter, while translate loads just the current locale, so translations outside requests (jobs, mailers) cannot fall back to the site default or English.

The translation cache key does not include the site or its default locale, but fallback results now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, so multisite processes or a changed default locale serve stale fallback translations.

findings.description: Rejected device stays in cache, bypassing the anonymous device limit — The rejected device's next request within the 29-minute cache TTL passes the cache check, so `Authenticate` grants it anonymous access and the limit is bypassed. Call `localCache.Delete(key)` in `tagDeviceUI` when `CreateOrUpdateDevice` fails, or set the entry only after a successful write.

Device limit check is racy: COUNT then unconditional upsert can exceed limit — Concurrent requests from new devices can all read a count below `deviceLimit` and all insert, so the limit is exceeded. Make the `CountDevices` check and the insert atomic, for example with a conditional `INSERT ... SELECT` or a serialized transaction.

`TagDevice` now runs synchronously in `Authenticate`, slowing anonymous requests — Every uncached device now adds a COUNT query and an upsert to the request path, even when `device_limit` is 0, so slow DB writes delay requests and request cancellation aborts tagging. Keep tagging asynchronous when no limit is set, and run it synchronously only when `AnonymousDeviceLimit > 0`.

goldensDetail.text: tagDeviceUI caches the device key before CreateOrUpdateDevice; when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the entry stays, so the next request from the same device skips the limit check and authenticates for up to 29 minutes.
The new auth.anonymous device_limit setting has no entry in conf/defaults.ini, so the GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT environment override is ignored and the limit stays 0.

findings.description: Missing cache re-check after acquiring write lock causes redundant manifest reloads — During a cold cache in non-dev mode, every waiting request re-reads and re-parses the manifest one at a time under the write lock. After `Lock()`, re-check `cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil` and return `entryPointAssetsCache` if it is set.

Async legacy create write uses request context that is cancelled on return — The request `ctx` is cancelled once the handler returns, so the background write can abort mid-flight and leave the legacy store out of sync. Derive the timeout from `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)`, and apply the same fix in the `Update`, `Delete` and `DeleteCollection` goroutines.

Delete success metric uses object name as label, causing unbounded cardinality — Using `name` as a label value creates one metric series per deleted object, which means unbounded cardinality and metrics inconsistent with other calls. Pass `options.Kind` instead, and use the enriched `log` rather than `d.Log` when setting the context logger.

Async legacy update uses raw objInfo instead of the object Storage persisted — Passing the raw `objInfo` lets `Legacy.Update` recompute the change against its own old copy after the request ends, so legacy can store different content than Storage. Wrap the result as `updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: res}` before the goroutine and pass that to `Legacy.Update`.

Failed storage Create recorded as legacy duration instead of storage duration — Recording a failed Storage create with `recordLegacyDuration` pollutes the legacy metrics and leaves the storage error metric empty. Call `recordStorageDuration(true, ...)` instead.

**Also found in:**
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:127-131`
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:161-167`

goldensDetail.text: The legacy DeleteCollection goroutine records its duration with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, misattributing legacy latency and errors to the storage metric.
Delete's success path records the storage metric with the object name in the kind label instead of options.Kind, creating per-object series and inconsistent labels.
On storage Create/Update failure the duration is recorded with recordLegacyDuration, attributing unified-store errors to the legacy metric.

Mode 3 legacy writes now run in background goroutines derived from the request context, which is cancelled when the request completes, so legacy writes can be cancelled and legacy storage falls out of sync.
Legacy.Update now receives the original objInfo instead of a wrapper carrying the object stored in unified storage, so legacy recomputes the update and can diverge.
The Mode 3 tests never wait for or assert the asynchronous legacy writes, and legacy and storage share one mock, so removing the legacy calls would not fail them.
Independent per-request goroutines remove ordering between legacy writes to the same resource, so legacy can end up with an older version or a resurrected object.
Mode 3 legacy-storage write errors (create/update/delete/delete-collection) are no longer logged after moving to async goroutines; only a duration metric with an error flag is recorded.
DualWriterMode3.Delete now returns on any unified-storage error, including NotFound, before deleting from legacy, so objects that exist only in legacy can no longer be deleted.

findings.description: Unlocked TotalDocs cache iteration races with event goroutine's index creation — Iterating `bleveBackend.cache` without `cacheMu` can race with `BuildIndex` writes from the event goroutine, causing a fatal concurrent map iteration and write at startup. Take `cacheMu.RLock()` inside `bleveBackend.TotalDocs()`.

Concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key race on index creation — Without the `cacheMu` lock, concurrent `BuildIndex` calls for one key can make the second `bleve.New(dir)` fail on file-backed indexes, or overwrite and leak an in-memory index. Serialize builds per key (a per-key mutex or singleflight) and re-check the cache after acquiring it.

goldensDetail.text: BuildIndex now locks only the final cache assignment, so concurrent callers for the same uncached key all build the same expensive index in parallel and the last one overwrites the others.

The new startup log calls TotalDocs, which iterates the index cache without a lock, after the event goroutine that can add indexes has started, so a concurrent map read and write can crash the process.
The PR skips the storage-server module integration test on postgres instead of fixing the failure, removing coverage of the new eager initialization on postgres.

findings.description: GrafanaRuleListItem rendered in list without a key prop — Without a key, React reconciles these items by index, so loading more results or re-sorting can mis-associate component state across rules. Add `key={key}` to `GrafanaRuleListItem`, as the other branches do with the `key` already destructured.

Legacy useAllAlertRuleAbilities no longer treats federated rules as immutable — `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` hard-codes `isFederated = false`, so federated Mimir rules are no longer immutable for Update, Delete and Pause in every legacy caller. Compute `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` in `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` and pass it to the shared implementation.

Duplicate ability granted when Grafana prom rule is undefined (skipToken) — When `rule` is undefined, `MaybeSupported` still grants Duplicate, and `AlertRuleMenu` ORs it with the ruler ability, so datasource rules show Duplicate to users who only have Grafana create permission. Make `MaybeSupported` resolve to `NotSupported` when `rule` is missing.

goldensDetail.text: The pause menu item is still gated on a Grafana ruler rule, but the list view now passes only the Prometheus rule, so Pause/Resume disappears for list-view rules even when the user may pause them.
The Delete menu item still requires a ruler rule, which list-view Grafana rules no longer provide, so users with delete permission lose the Delete action.

When the Grafana prom-rule branch is skipped (datasource rules), useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) still reports Duplicate as supported and allowed by Grafana create permission, and AlertRuleMenu ORs it with the ruler ability, so Duplicate appears on cloud rules even when the ruler check denies it.

For list-view Grafana rules RuleActionsButtons gets only promRule, so the Silence menu item is shown but the silence drawer, still gated on a ruler alerting rule, never renders and clicking Silence does nothing.

findings.description: isAccessTokenId matcher checks wrong substring and inverts grant comparison — The matcher accepts any `xxxxxx:uuid`-shaped value and never validates the grant type, so tests using it can pass wrongly. Read the shortcut with `substring(4, 6)` and return false when it differs from `expectedGrantShortcut`, also checking the length is 6.

rawTokenId null check validates grantType instead of rawTokenId — A null `rawTokenId` passes validation and yields ids like `onrtac:null` from `encodeTokenId` instead of failing fast. Call `Objects.requireNonNull` on `rawTokenId` rather than `grantType`.

The reader thread is never joined before `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` — A request still in flight after `deletedAll.set(true)` can throw after the assertion runs, so the test can pass while the NPE still occurs. Keep the `Thread` reference and call `join()` after `deletedAll.set(true)`, before `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())`.

Lithuanian totpStep1 contains Italian text instead of Lithuanian — Lithuanian users see Italian text in the TOTP setup step. Replace `totpStep1` with a Lithuanian translation, and fix `loginTotpStep1` in the login `messages_lt.properties`, which has the same Italian sentence.

zh_CN totpStep1 uses Traditional Chinese text instead of Simplified — Simplified Chinese users see Traditional characters and wording in the TOTP setup step. Change `totpStep1` to the Simplified text, "在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：".

Overlapping prefix/suffix trimming causes StringIndexOutOfBoundsException — When the matched prefix and suffix overlap, `substring` throws `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException`, so the verifier crashes instead of reporting the illegal HTML. Cap `end` at the shorter length of `value` and `sanitized` minus `start`.

goldensDetail.text: The diff-trimming code computes common prefix and suffix independently, so they can overlap and substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the verifier instead of reporting the illegal HTML.

The account and admin UI bundles now use Java MessageFormat placeholders and choice syntax for error-invalid-multivalued-size, but i18next expects {{n}}, so the UI shows literal {0}/{1}/{2} and the raw choice text.

findings.description: canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, crashing token exchange in V2 — With V2 enabled, `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` returns this class, so `AbstractTokenExchangeProvider` hits an uncaught `UnsupportedOperationException` on every cross-audience exchange. Return `false` instead so the caller produces the normal 403 response.

getClientsWithPermission may miss per-client resources and include the type resource — Per-client resources made by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` have no type, so `resourceStore.findByType` likely skips them, and `AvailableRoleMappingResource` loses those clients. Iterate per-client resources by name or owner, or set the type there, and skip the "Clients" type resource.

goldensDetail.text: Claims the removal-cleanup listener is guarded by the V1 fine-grained flag, so client/role/group permissions are orphaned when V1 is disabled or only V2 is enabled.

getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 only finds the type-level 'Clients' resource and returns its name, never actual client ids, so callers that resolve the returned values as client ids get wrong results or null clients.
Claims getResourceTypeResource can return null in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, causing a NullPointerException in findByResource.
ClientPermissionsV2.canView() ignores a global MANAGE permission, so admins with only global manage take the unpaginated, per-client evaluated listing path.
canView(client) short-circuits on the global all-clients VIEW permission, so a client-specific permission denying an admin is never evaluated and the client is still viewable.

The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, an admin granted a permission on all clients is denied on any client that also has its own per-client permission resource, because only the per-client resource is evaluated.

ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AbstractTokenExchangeProvider still calls clients().canExchangeTo for client-to-client exchange, so with token exchange and FGAP V2 enabled the request fails with a server error instead of a permission decision.
The test registers cleanup for the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases, so the created identity providers are never cleaned up.

Adding the organization/BROKER_PUBLIC check to the shared LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate also changes IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate, so with organizations disabled a user's linked IdP that has an organizationId but is not public is no longer shown on the login page.

findings.description: Error timestamps in seconds compared with replay timestamps in milliseconds — Every error sorts before the first replay event, so the log sent to Seer is no longer chronological. Normalize the units, for example by multiplying the error timestamp by 1000 or by dividing the `timestamp` of each replay event by 1000.

Age/timestamp exclusivity check misses zero values and absent fields — Truthiness checks in `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` accept `age=0` or `timestamp=0` alongside the other field, and a report with neither field passes. Replace them with a `validate()` method that checks key presence in `attrs` and requires exactly one.

goldensDetail.text: The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators check truthiness via initial_data.get(), so a zero value is treated as absent and a report carrying both fields passes validation.
The validation-failure warning logs the entire raw, attacker-controlled browser report instead of a redacted subset.
The Snuba replay lookup for error IDs runs even when enable_error_context=false, adding a needless query (and failure point) to opt-out requests.

With the use-table-widget-visualization flag on, the widget renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded empty columns and data instead of the query results, so every table widget shows an empty table.
The custom cell renderers fall back to default rendering on any falsy return (0, '', null), not only undefined, so a renderer cannot render zero or an empty cell.
The attribute-keys query key no longer includes the organization slug, so two organizations with the same filters share a cache entry and switching orgs can show the previous org's attribute names.

Every paginated breadcrumb-summary request queries the replay and fetches all of its error events from nodestore with no cap, adding latency and memory proportional to the replay's error count on each page.
HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES is applied only when a search query is present; the no-search early return shows all attributes, so the hidden attributes still appear in the default span attributes view.

The bulk delete test sets max_segment_id to None to cover the new guard in _make_recording_filenames, but it mocks delete_matched_rows, so the guard is never executed and removing it would not fail the test.
Error event timestamps (seconds) are compared with replay recording event timestamps (milliseconds), so errors are not interleaved chronologically with breadcrumbs.

findings.description: join() skips terminate() for remaining processes after deadline expires — Flusher processes still running after the deadline stay alive after shutdown, because `join()` skips `process.terminate()` for them. Remove the early `break` so every `multiprocessing.Process` is terminated.

get_memory_info() queried once per buffer, scanning shared Redis N times — Each `SpansBuffer` wraps the same Redis cluster, so calling `get_memory_info()` per buffer scans it N times on every `submit()`. Query only one buffer from `self.buffers` instead of looping over all of them.

The test patches `time.sleep` to a no-op at the top, so the added `time.sleep(0.1)` does not wait — Because the test patches `time.sleep` to a no-op, the added `time.sleep(0.1)` never waits, so `step.join()` can stop the flusher before it flushes and make `(msg,) = messages` flaky. Capture the real sleep before patching, or poll until `messages` is non-empty with a timeout.

goldensDetail.text: The restart path only kills a hung flusher if it is a multiprocessing.Process, but spawn-context workers are SpawnProcess, so hung processes are never killed and a duplicate flusher is started for the same shards.
join() breaks out of the per-process loop when the shared deadline expires, skipping termination of the remaining flusher processes and leaving them running after shutdown.

findings.description: Dataclass default `timezone.now()` is evaluated once at import time — Every `AssignmentSource` gets the same stale import-time timestamp in `queued`, so the serialized value is wrong for anything that relies on it. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead, importing `field` from `dataclasses`.

OAuth `state` is the constant `pipeline.signature`, giving no CSRF protection — Because `pipeline.signature` is identical for every user and session, an attacker can send a victim a setup URL with the attacker's own `code`, binding the attacker's login and defeating the new user-match check. Generate a random per-flow nonce, store it in the pipeline state, and compare against it instead of `pipeline.signature`.

KeyError when integration metadata lacks sender login — Existing integrations without `sender` metadata raise `KeyError` on `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`, returning a 500 instead of the error page. Use `.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and return `error(...)` when it is missing.

Installer verification skipped when no Integration row exists yet — When no `Integration` row exists yet, `pipeline.next_step()` runs without the user-match check, so racing the installation webhook bypasses verification. Fail closed in the `Integration.DoesNotExist` branch, or verify the installer through the GitHub API.

Network errors in GitHub OAuth token exchange and user lookup cause unhandled 500 — `safe_urlopen` and `get_user_info` run outside the try/except, so network errors, timeouts or `ApiError` from GitHub surface as an unhandled 500 mid-pipeline. Wrap both calls and return `error(request, self.active_organization)` on failure.

goldensDetail.text: test_installation_not_found uses a wrong OAuth state, so it fails at the state check and never reaches the installation-not-found path it is meant to test.

findings.description: MetricAlertDetectorHandler leaves StatefulDetectorHandler abstract methods unimplemented — Instantiating `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` via `Detector.detector_handler` raises `TypeError` because `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` and `build_occurrence_and_event_data` are abstract, which crashes `process_detectors` for every `metric_alert_fire` detector. Implement those methods, or restore the stub `evaluate` returning `{}` until the stateful handler is built.

goldensDetail.text: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing its abstract methods, so instantiating it for metric alert detectors raises TypeError where it previously returned an empty-result handler.

The mock occurrence builder ignores its value argument, so tests (e.g. group_2 expected with 6 while the packet carries 10) pass regardless of which value is passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data.

findings.description: Monitor context returns raw config instead of computed config copy — The occurrence context carries the raw numeric `schedule_type` because the computed `config` copy built in `get_monitor_environment_context` is discarded. Return `config` instead of `monitor_environment.monitor.config` in the `"config"` field.

TypeError on mainHostDestinationCalendar when destinationCalendar is empty — An empty or null `evt.destinationCalendar` triggers an unhandled `TypeError` during Google Meet bookings. Use optional chaining on `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration` to safely fall back to Daily video.

Inverted condition for setting organization slug — Disabling billing drops `slug`, while enabling billing incorrectly assigns both `slug` and `requestedSlug`. Revert the condition on `slug` to check `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`.

destinationCalendar initialized to null drops team calendars — Collective bookings silently drop team members' calendars when the organizer lacks a destination calendar. Default `destinationCalendar` to an empty array instead of `null` so `push` can append `teamDestinationCalendars`.

Fallback calendar lookup searches by falsy externalCalendarId — Because `externalCalendarId` is falsy in the fallback branch, `selectedCalendar` always resolves to `undefined`. Default directly to `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId` instead.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:315-317`

goldensDetail.text: When externalCalendarId is absent, updateEvent/deleteEvent look for a destination calendar whose externalId equals that absent value, so the lookup never matches and the configured destination calendar is no longer used.
The organization slug is now set only when team billing is enabled (inverted condition), so with billing both slug and requestedSlug are set and without billing neither is.

Office365 (and Lark) createEvent ignore the new credentialId argument and always use the first destination calendar, so in collective bookings other hosts' credentials target the organizer's calendar instead of their own.

The Google Meet fallback reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining, so a Meet booking with a null or empty destinationCalendar throws instead of falling back to Cal Video.

For collective events whose organizer has no destination calendar, destinationCalendar is null and the optional push drops all other hosts' destination calendars, so those hosts never get calendar events.
Video booking references are now saved without their credentialId, so cancelling the booking can no longer find the video credential and the meeting is not deleted.

Cancelling all remaining occurrences of a recurring collective booking deletes only the first calendar reference of each booking, repeated once per host, so the other hosts' events stay on their calendars.

In Google createEvent, when no destination calendar matches the credentialId, the hangout-link events.patch is called with an undefined calendarId and fails, so the Meet link is not added to the event description.

When cancelling a recurring booking with multiple calendar references, the recurring-event deletion over all remaining bookings and credentials runs once per reference, causing duplicate delete calls and errors.

findings.description: Team admin or owner check uses logical AND instead of OR — Administrators who are not owners are incorrectly rejected with a forbidden error. Use `||` instead of `&&` to combine `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner`, or check `isTeamAdmin` alone if it already verifies both roles.

goldensDetail.text: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, so only team owners pass; team admins who are not organizer or attendee are wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN.

The guest blacklist is lowercased but incoming guest emails are compared without normalization, so a blacklisted address submitted with different casing bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and is added and emailed.
The server never deduplicates the guests array, so a request with the same email twice inserts duplicate attendee rows for the booking.

The handler passes the unfiltered guests list to sendAddGuestsEmails, which uses it to pick who gets AttendeeScheduledEmail, so existing attendees included in the request receive a new-booking confirmation instead of the add-guests email.

EventManager is created with the requesting user's credentials, so when a non-organizer adds guests the organizer's calendar event is not updated (or the wrong account is used) for references without a credentialId.
sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings, so hosts and attendees receive add-guests emails even when standard emails are disabled.

The add-guests handler omits booking.iCalUID from the CalendarEvent, so the add-guests emails' .ics attachments use booking.uid as UID and recipients' calendars treat them as a new event rather than an update of the original booking invite.
Guest email uniqueness is checked case-sensitively, so case variants of the same address are accepted as distinct guests (and slip past the lowercased blacklist).

findings.description: Zod safe-parse wrapper stored in credential key — Subsequent reads parsing `credential.key` with `googleCredentialSchema` will throw validation errors because the `{ success: true, data: ... }` wrapper is saved instead of the payload. Pass `key.data` instead of `key` to `prisma.credential.update`.

Credential ID passed to refreshOAuthTokens instead of user ID — The sync service associates token refreshes with the wrong account or fails resolution because `credentialId` is forwarded as `calcomUserId`. Pass `credential.userId` instead, or update `refreshAccessToken` to receive and forward the user ID.

Raw fetch Response breaks callers expecting Axios data or token payload — Callers accessing `.data` on the returned `Response` receive `undefined` and throw a `TypeError` when credential sync is enabled. Parse and return the JSON payload from `response` instead of returning the raw Fetch `Response`.

Case-sensitive header lookup and non-constant-time secret comparison — Node.js lowercases all `req.headers` keys, causing mixed-case lookups to fail, while `!==` leaves the secret vulnerable to timing attacks. Convert `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` to lowercase before indexing and compare the secret using `crypto.timingSafeEqual`.

Using `z.string().toString()` produces `[object Object]` schema keys — This strips token response properties other than `access_token` and skips expiry validation because `z.string().toString()` evaluates to the literal key `"[object Object]"`. Replace the computed keys with `z.record()` or chain `.passthrough()` on the schema.

goldensDetail.text: The webhook parses the body with zod .parse and decrypts/JSON-parses the keys without error handling, so invalid payloads produce 500 errors instead of 400 responses.
parseRefreshTokenResponse writes the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when the refresh response omits a refresh token, so the stored credential gets an invalid refresh token and later refreshes fail.

minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys from z.string().toString(), which produce a literal key rather than a wildcard, so the sync-mode schema does not validate or keep expiry and other token fields as intended.
Google Calendar persists the safeParse result object instead of its data as the credential key, corrupting the stored credential so later reads fail.
Salesforce getClient now refreshes the OAuth token and writes the credential on every service construction, adding a network round trip and DB write even when the access token is valid.
The new Salesforce token refresh uses prisma without importing it, so the code fails type checking and throws a ReferenceError at runtime.
Salesforce checks response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok when refreshing the token, which can misclassify successful responses, and then ignores the refreshed token.
After refreshing the Salesforce token, jsforce.Connection is created with the stale access_token and instance_url instead of the newly refreshed values.

The app-credential webhook looks up appStoreMetadata by app.slug, but the map is keyed by dirName, so apps whose slug differs from their directory (e.g. google-calendar) always get a 404 and their credentials cannot be synced.

findings.description: Deletion query matches non-SMS reminders when retry count exceeds 1 — Non-SMS workflows like email or WhatsApp will be unintentionally deleted after repeated retries. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to this condition or move the method filter into the parent `where` clause.

goldensDetail.text: retryCount is set to reminder.retryCount + 1 from a value read at the start of the run instead of an atomic increment, so overlapping runs can lose increments.
The deleteMany OR clause applies retryCount > 1 without the SMS method filter, so the SMS cron deletes any workflow reminder (email, WhatsApp) with retryCount above 1.

The retry-count update inside the catch block is not guarded, so if it throws (for example the reminder was deleted concurrently) the error escapes the loop and the cron run fails, skipping the remaining reminders.
Claims transient errors increment retryCount, so two runs during an outage delete the whole pending SMS reminder queue.

SMS-sending locks are counted as failed scheduling attempts: scheduleSMS returns undefined for locked users/teams, retryCount is incremented, and after two cron runs the retryCount > 1 cleanup deletes future reminders even if sending is later unlocked.

The credentials authorize() skips the password check when any totpCode is present, and the new backup-code branch never validates that totpCode, so a backup code plus a dummy totpCode logs in without the account password.
The getBaseConditions test uses a single booking matching both auth and filter conditions, so it would pass even if the conditions were not combined.
The new public options type makes teamId optional for team scope, so a missing teamId compiles and silently yields empty insights instead of a type error.
Claims getBaseConditions returns OR fragments without parentheses, so a caller appending `AND <extra>` would leak rows outside the authorization scope.

findings.description: Invalid `<%- end if %>` tag causes syntax error — Rendering this view crashes with a 500 internal server error during template compilation. Replace `<%- end if %>` with `<%- end %>`.

NoMethodError when feed item lacks content element — Feeds omitting the `<content>` tag crash when `scrub` is called on `nil`. Fall back to `i.description` when `i.content` is absent before calling `scrub`.

XSS vulnerability from unescaped request.referer in script tag — A manipulated `Referer` header can execute arbitrary JavaScript in the user's browser. Sanitize `request.referer` with `escape_javascript` or serialize it with `to_json`.

Topic retrieval expectation checks synchronous execution instead of Jobs.enqueue — This test fails because `EmbedController#best` delegates topic retrieval asynchronously. Assert that `Jobs.expects(:enqueue).with(:retrieve_topic, ...)` is called instead of mocking `TopicRetriever`.

goldensDetail.text: The referer and embed_url host checks compare against SiteSetting.embeddable_host case-sensitively, so a host differing only in case is rejected even though hostnames are case-insensitive.

PollFeed reads i.content.scrub for every feed item, so items without a content element (common in RSS feeds that only have description) raise NoMethodError and abort the import of the remaining items.

TopicEmbed.import appends a footer that interpolates the URL unescaped into an <a href='...'> tag in raw HTML that is later rendered unsanitized, so a crafted URL can inject markup; it also appends to contents with << without handling nil.
When the embedded post has been deleted, TopicEmbed.import's update path passes a nil embed.post to PostRevisor and crashes on every later import of that URL.
Claims import_remote crashes on unparseable pages (nil content) and dead URLs because it does no nil check or network error handling around open(url).read.

absolutize_urls only handles root-relative paths: protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/x.png are rewritten to http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png and path-relative links are left unresolved, breaking links and images in imported posts.

Every retrieval of an article not yet embedded synchronously polls and imports the entire RSS feed, and since throttling is per URL, many different article requests repeat the full feed download and processing.

The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' specs leave feed_polling_enabled at its false default, so they never reach the condition they name and would pass with those checks deleted.
`import_remote` fetches the embed URL with open-uri, which follows redirects, so the embeddable-host check on the initial URL can be bypassed to reach internal services (SSRF).
The retrieve throttle is keyed by the full embed URL, so an anonymous client can vary the query string on the embeddable host to bypass it and make the server create an unbounded number of topics.

The "requires feed_polling_enabled?" spec leaves feed_polling_url and embed_by_username at their blank defaults, so poll_feed is skipped regardless and the test would pass even without the enabled check.
The embed layout references the 'embed' stylesheet and embed.js, but neither is in config.assets.precompile, so with precompiled assets in production the embed page fails to load them.

findings.description: NoMethodError when category settings are absent from site_settings — Missing `embed_category` or `uncategorized_category_id` records in `site_settings` crash the migration when indexing the empty query result. Check `cmd_tuples` on the result before accessing `[0]`.

Calling sub! raises NoMethodError when host is nil — A `nil` `host` crashes the callback before validation can handle it. Guard the `sub!` calls with `self.host.present?` so missing hosts fail validation cleanly.

goldensDetail.text: The migration reads execute(...)[0]['id'] for embed_category without checking for an empty result, so installs without that setting stored crash the migration instead of falling back to the uncategorized category.

After saving a host, the component overwrites its category with findById(categoryId); when no category was chosen this is null even though the server saved the uncategorized category, so the row shows no category until reload.
Hosts saved with a port (allowed by the validation regex) are stored as host:port, but lookup compares only URI.host, so those configured hosts never match and embedding fails for them.
EmbeddableHost's host format validation only accepts TLDs of 2-5 letters, so admins cannot add embeddable hosts on longer TLDs like example.technology.

The flex-item styles target the inner .extra-info-wrapper instead of the component's root div, so in the flexbox header a long topic title keeps its full width and pushes the navigation panel out instead of being truncated.
The align-items mixin emits no -moz-box-align, so on old Firefox versions using the display:-moz-box fallback the advertised vertical centering is not applied.

Removing the float-based right alignment of .d-header .panel leaves the server-rendered (no-JS) header's login panel, which sits inside .row and is not a flex item, no longer right-aligned next to the title.

Making .small-action a flex container leaves .small-action-desc content-sized (no flex:1), so the right-floated edit/delete buttons inside it sit right after short action descriptions instead of at the right edge of the row.

On mobile the .small-action custom message keeps margin-left:-40px, tuned for the old 4em left padding; with the new flex layout and 1.5% padding it is pulled into the avatar column and overlaps the icon.

findings.description: Duplicate self.downsize definition overwrites multi-argument version — Callers like `Jobs::ResizeEmoji` that pass width and height separately will raise an `ArgumentError`. Consolidate `self.downsize` into a single method that handles both dimension strings and numeric arguments.

Hardcoded maxSizeKB bypasses attachment size limit — Non-image attachments bypass client-side size restrictions even though the server cannot automatically downsize them. Check `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_attachment_size_kb` when `type` is `'attachment'` and apply the 10MB `maxSizeKB` limit only for `'image'`.

goldensDetail.text: downsize is defined twice in OptimizedImage; the new (from, to, dimensions, opts) version overrides the (max_width, max_height) one, so existing callers such as ResizeEmoji that pass width and height now raise ArgumentError.

The client-side upload size check hardcodes 10 MB instead of the per-type max_<type>_size_kb setting, so attachment limits diverge from the server: larger allowed attachments are blocked and smaller limits are only enforced server-side.
The upload downsizing passes a percentage ('80%') as dimensions, but for animated GIFs the gifsicle path uses --resize-fit, which expects WxH geometry, so downsizing silently fails.
Auto-downsizing passes the upload tempfile path, which lacks a .gif extension, so the animated branch is never chosen and convert keeps only the first frame, flattening oversized animated GIFs.
Claims the downsize loop checking tempfile.size may never terminate because of a stale cached size, causing infinite loops.
Oversized SVG uploads go through the new ImageMagick downsize loop because SVG counts as an image, so the vector file is rasterized or corrupted in place before Upload.create_for parses it as SVG.

The upload tempfile path, which for API URL uploads embeds the request-controlled type param, is now passed to OptimizedImage.downsize and run unescaped in a shell via backticks, allowing command injection through type.
The 413 upload error message states a hard-coded 10 MB maximum that may not match the limit the server or web server actually enforces.

findings.description: Group membership actions expect :group_id instead of :id in params — Requests to `/admin/groups/:id/members.json` fail with `ActionController::ParameterMissing` because the member routes provide `params[:id]`. Read the group identifier from `params[:id] || params[:group_id]` in `add_members` and `remove_member`.

totalPages overcounts pages when user_count is a multiple of limit — This leaves `showingLast` false and allows users to paginate to an empty trailing page. Compute `totalPages` using `Math.ceil` instead of adding one to `Math.floor`.

goldensDetail.text: The admin group pager computes total pages as floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so when the member count is an exact multiple of the limit it shows an extra page and Next navigates to an empty member list.
Paging actions fire overlapping member requests and each response unconditionally overwrites offset and members, so a stale response arriving last can revert the list to an earlier page.
The public members endpoint now always caps results at 50 per page, but the public group members page has no pagination, so groups with more than 50 members are silently truncated for users.
Creating a group ignores the alias_level the admin selected, saving only name and visibility, so new groups keep the default alias level.
Removing a member deletes the membership row directly and skips clearing the user's primary_group_id, so a removed user can keep this group as their primary group.
Group member pagination is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit: Next moves to offset == user_count and shows an empty page.
Admin remove_member deletes memberships with group.users.delete, which skips GroupUser callbacks, so the cached groups.user_count is never decremented and stays inflated.

Admin add_members pushes every username into group.users without skipping existing members, so adding someone already in the group hits the unique group_users index, returns a 500 and leaves earlier users partially added.
The public group members endpoint takes `limit` from params with no upper bound or positivity check, letting a visitor request huge pages or trigger a 500 with a negative limit.
Admin remove_member calls group.users.delete with a raw integer id, which raises RecordNotFound (404/500) when the user is not or no longer a member, e.g. on concurrent removal.

Fallback locale catalogs are only loaded in the controller's set_locale filter, while translate loads just the current locale, so translations outside requests (jobs, mailers) cannot fall back to the site default or English.

The translation cache key does not include the site or its default locale, but fallback results now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, so multisite processes or a changed default locale serve stale fallback translations.

findings.description: Premature cache entry permits rejected devices to bypass limit — Devices rejected with `ErrDeviceLimitReached` bypass limits on subsequent requests because `tagDeviceUI` populates `localCache` before `CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds. Only insert into `localCache` after `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns without error, or evict the key on failure.

goldensDetail.text: tagDeviceUI caches the device key before CreateOrUpdateDevice; when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the entry stays, so the next request from the same device skips the limit check and authenticates for up to 29 minutes.
The new auth.anonymous device_limit setting has no entry in conf/defaults.ini, so the GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT environment override is ignored and the limit stays 0.

findings.description: Missing double-checked locking after acquiring write lock — Concurrent callers queued on `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()` will redundantly re-parse the manifest and risk overwriting a valid cache with `nil`. Re-check `entryPointAssetsCache` and `cfg.Env` immediately after acquiring the lock to return early.

High cardinality metric label from passing object name as kind — Using individual resource identifiers causes unbounded metric cardinality and memory growth in Prometheus. Pass `options.Kind` instead of `name` to `d.recordStorageDuration`.

Legacy DeleteCollection records duration in unified storage metrics — Recording legacy deletions under unified metrics skews latency and error rate measurements across both storage systems. Call `d.recordLegacyDuration` instead of `d.recordStorageDuration`.

DualWriterMode3.Create records storage errors to legacy duration metric — Recording storage failures to legacy metrics distorts error rate and latency observability across both backends. Call `d.recordStorageDuration` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration`.

**Also found in:**
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:127-131`

goldensDetail.text: The legacy DeleteCollection goroutine records its duration with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, misattributing legacy latency and errors to the storage metric.
Delete's success path records the storage metric with the object name in the kind label instead of options.Kind, creating per-object series and inconsistent labels.
On storage Create/Update failure the duration is recorded with recordLegacyDuration, attributing unified-store errors to the legacy metric.

Mode 3 legacy writes now run in background goroutines derived from the request context, which is cancelled when the request completes, so legacy writes can be cancelled and legacy storage falls out of sync.
Legacy.Update now receives the original objInfo instead of a wrapper carrying the object stored in unified storage, so legacy recomputes the update and can diverge.
The Mode 3 tests never wait for or assert the asynchronous legacy writes, and legacy and storage share one mock, so removing the legacy calls would not fail them.
Independent per-request goroutines remove ordering between legacy writes to the same resource, so legacy can end up with an older version or a resurrected object.
Mode 3 legacy-storage write errors (create/update/delete/delete-collection) are no longer logged after moving to async goroutines; only a duration metric with an error flag is recorded.
DualWriterMode3.Delete now returns on any unified-storage error, including NotFound, before deleting from legacy, so objects that exist only in legacy can no longer be deleted.
BuildIndex now locks only the final cache assignment, so concurrent callers for the same uncached key all build the same expensive index in parallel and the last one overwrites the others.

The new startup log calls TotalDocs, which iterates the index cache without a lock, after the event goroutine that can add indexes has started, so a concurrent map read and write can crash the process.
The PR skips the storage-server module integration test on postgres instead of fixing the failure, removing coverage of the new eager initialization on postgres.

findings.description: Missing `key` prop on GrafanaRuleListItem — Omitting this causes React reconciliation bugs and console warnings when the list reorders or filters update. Pass `key={key}` to `GrafanaRuleListItem`.

goldensDetail.text: The pause menu item is still gated on a Grafana ruler rule, but the list view now passes only the Prometheus rule, so Pause/Resume disappears for list-view rules even when the user may pause them.
The Delete menu item still requires a ruler rule, which list-view Grafana rules no longer provide, so users with delete permission lose the Delete action.

When the Grafana prom-rule branch is skipped (datasource rules), useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) still reports Duplicate as supported and allowed by Grafana create permission, and AlertRuleMenu ORs it with the ruler ability, so Duplicate appears on cloud rules even when the ruler check denies it.

For list-view Grafana rules RuleActionsButtons gets only promRule, so the Silence menu item is shown but the silence drawer, still gated on a ruler alerting rule, never renders and clicking Silence does nothing.

findings.description: Duplicate null check on grantType instead of rawTokenId — Passing `null` for `rawTokenId` slips through unvalidated and can cause null dereferences downstream. Update the second `Objects.requireNonNull` call to check `rawTokenId` instead of `grantType`.

isAccessTokenId inverts grant check and uses wrong substring indices — The inverted condition and shifted substring allow mismatched events to pass tests without asserting the grant shortcut. Update the check to return `false` when `items[0].substring(4, 6)` does not match `expectedGrantShortcut`.

Background thread never joined before asserting test results — An in-flight request can throw after `assertThat` runs or leak into subsequent test runs. Retain a reference to the `Thread` and call `join()` after updating `deletedAll`.

getSubGroupsCount returns null when model is null — Callers risk a `NullPointerException` upon unboxing because `GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount` contractually never returns `null`. Return `0L` instead of `null` when `model` is missing.

Overlapping prefix and suffix cause StringIndexOutOfBoundsException — When `start + end` exceeds the string length, calling `substring` crashes theme verification. Bound `end` in the `while` loop condition using `sanitized.length() - start` and `value.length() - start`.

goldensDetail.text: The diff-trimming code computes common prefix and suffix independently, so they can overlap and substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the verifier instead of reporting the illegal HTML.

The account and admin UI bundles now use Java MessageFormat placeholders and choice syntax for error-invalid-multivalued-size, but i18next expects {{n}}, so the UI shows literal {0}/{1}/{2} and the raw choice text.

findings.description: setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException on client removal — Client deletion fails during the synchronous `ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent` listener in `AdminPermissions`. Make `setPermissionsEnabled` a no-op here or guard `AdminPermissions.registerListener` against invoking V2 evaluators.

goldensDetail.text: Claims the removal-cleanup listener is guarded by the V1 fine-grained flag, so client/role/group permissions are orphaned when V1 is disabled or only V2 is enabled.

getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 only finds the type-level 'Clients' resource and returns its name, never actual client ids, so callers that resolve the returned values as client ids get wrong results or null clients.
Claims getResourceTypeResource can return null in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, causing a NullPointerException in findByResource.
ClientPermissionsV2.canView() ignores a global MANAGE permission, so admins with only global manage take the unpaginated, per-client evaluated listing path.
canView(client) short-circuits on the global all-clients VIEW permission, so a client-specific permission denying an admin is never evaluated and the client is still viewable.

The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, an admin granted a permission on all clients is denied on any client that also has its own per-client permission resource, because only the per-client resource is evaluated.

ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AbstractTokenExchangeProvider still calls clients().canExchangeTo for client-to-client exchange, so with token exchange and FGAP V2 enabled the request fails with a server error instead of a permission decision.
The test registers cleanup for the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases, so the created identity providers are never cleaned up.

Adding the organization/BROKER_PUBLIC check to the shared LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate also changes IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate, so with organizations disabled a user's linked IdP that has an organizationId but is not public is no longer shown on the login page.

findings.description: Misaligned error IDs and nodestore events when zipping events.values() — Missing keys or unexpected ordering from nodestore will associate event payloads with the wrong IDs. Look up each payload by `node_id` using `events.get(node_id)` instead of zipping `events.values()`.
