Age 0 and omitted fields bypass age and timestamp mutual exclusion — Truthiness checks with `.get()` treat `0` as absent, allowing invalid combinations or omitted fields to pass validation. Enforce mutual exclusion in serializer-level `validate()` using explicit key membership checks on `attrs`.

goldensDetail.text: The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators check truthiness via initial_data.get(), so a zero value is treated as absent and a report carrying both fields passes validation.
The validation-failure warning logs the entire raw, attacker-controlled browser report instead of a redacted subset.
The Snuba replay lookup for error IDs runs even when enable_error_context=false, adding a needless query (and failure point) to opt-out requests.

With the use-table-widget-visualization flag on, the widget renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded empty columns and data instead of the query results, so every table widget shows an empty table.
The custom cell renderers fall back to default rendering on any falsy return (0, '', null), not only undefined, so a renderer cannot render zero or an empty cell.
The attribute-keys query key no longer includes the organization slug, so two organizations with the same filters share a cache entry and switching orgs can show the previous org's attribute names.

Every paginated breadcrumb-summary request queries the replay and fetches all of its error events from nodestore with no cap, adding latency and memory proportional to the replay's error count on each page.
HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES is applied only when a search query is present; the no-search early return shows all attributes, so the hidden attributes still appear in the default span attributes view.

The bulk delete test sets max_segment_id to None to cover the new guard in _make_recording_filenames, but it mocks delete_matched_rows, so the guard is never executed and removing it would not fail the test.
Error event timestamps (seconds) are compared with replay recording event timestamps (milliseconds), so errors are not interleaved chronologically with breadcrumbs.

The restart path only kills a hung flusher if it is a multiprocessing.Process, but spawn-context workers are SpawnProcess, so hung processes are never killed and a duplicate flusher is started for the same shards.
join() breaks out of the per-process loop when the shared deadline expires, skipping termination of the remaining flusher processes and leaving them running after shutdown.

findings.description: `queued` default timestamp evaluated at module import time — All `AssignmentSource` instances share the process startup timestamp instead of recording when they were created. Set `queued` with `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so the timestamp evaluates upon each instantiation.

Pipeline advances without verifying user when Integration does not exist — An unauthorized user can complete the installation pipeline without identity verification if the integration record has not been created yet. Return `error(request, self.active_organization)` in the `Integration.DoesNotExist` block instead of calling `pipeline.next_step()`.

Unhandled KeyError or TypeError when accessing sender metadata — Missing or `None` sender metadata crashes the view with a 500 error instead of rendering the failure response. Safely retrieve the sender login from `integration.metadata` using `.get()` with an empty dictionary fallback.

goldensDetail.text: test_installation_not_found uses a wrong OAuth state, so it fails at the state check and never reaches the installation-not-found path it is meant to test.

MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing its abstract methods, so instantiating it for metric alert detectors raises TypeError where it previously returned an empty-result handler.

The mock occurrence builder ignores its value argument, so tests (e.g. group_2 expected with 6 while the packet carries 10) pass regardless of which value is passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data.

findings.description: Google Meet booking crashes when no destination calendar is set — Booking creation aborts instead of falling back to Cal Video because `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` dereferences an undefined calendar. Restore optional chaining on `mainHostDestinationCalendar`.

Video booking references lose credential IDs, preventing meeting deletion — `handleCancelBooking` skips video meeting deletion when the booking reference lacks `credentialId`. Preserve `result.credentialId` for video results as well as calendar results.

Collective bookings use the first host's destination calendar for every host — Other Office365 hosts can fail to create events or target the wrong calendar because `mainHostDestinationCalendar` selects the first destination despite each adapter invocation using different credentials. Select the destination matching the current credential, or pass a per-destination event from `createAllCalendarEvents`.

Missing external calendar IDs break legacy update and deletion routing — Legacy references without `externalCalendarId` cannot resolve `selectedCalendar`, while the equivalent deletion path incorrectly uses `primary` despite a configured non-primary destination. Restore a usable destination fallback for updates and deletions when `externalCalendarId` is absent.

Missing organizer calendar drops collective hosts' destination calendars — Other collective hosts lose their configured calendar events when the organizer has no destination, because `evt.destinationCalendar?.push` silently skips appending their destinations. Initialize `evt.destinationCalendar` as an array before appending `teamDestinationCalendars`.

Calendar location updates lose external calendar and credential IDs — `editLocationHandler` loses metadata needed to route later calendar operations because `CalendarManager.updateEvent` results contain neither `externalId` nor `credentialId`. Propagate the original reference's external calendar ID and credential ID through the update result before consuming them here.

Collective recurring cancellations leave other hosts' calendar events undeleted — Other hosts' recurring events remain undeleted because `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` limits deletion to the organizer and `updBooking.references.find` repeatedly selects the first calendar reference. Use `calendarCredential` for the current reference and match each updated booking's reference by `credentialId`.

Billing-disabled organization creation no longer saves a slug — `publishHandler` rejects publication when billing-disabled creation saves neither `slug` nor `metadata.requestedSlug`. Restore the `slug` assignment when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is false, leaving `requestedSlug` conditional on billing being enabled.

goldensDetail.text: When externalCalendarId is absent, updateEvent/deleteEvent look for a destination calendar whose externalId equals that absent value, so the lookup never matches and the configured destination calendar is no longer used.
The organization slug is now set only when team billing is enabled (inverted condition), so with billing both slug and requestedSlug are set and without billing neither is.

Office365 (and Lark) createEvent ignore the new credentialId argument and always use the first destination calendar, so in collective bookings other hosts' credentials target the organizer's calendar instead of their own.

The Google Meet fallback reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining, so a Meet booking with a null or empty destinationCalendar throws instead of falling back to Cal Video.

For collective events whose organizer has no destination calendar, destinationCalendar is null and the optional push drops all other hosts' destination calendars, so those hosts never get calendar events.
Video booking references are now saved without their credentialId, so cancelling the booking can no longer find the video credential and the meeting is not deleted.

Cancelling all remaining occurrences of a recurring collective booking deletes only the first calendar reference of each booking, repeated once per host, so the other hosts' events stay on their calendars.

In Google createEvent, when no destination calendar matches the credentialId, the hangout-link events.patch is called with an undefined calendarId and fails, so the Meet link is not added to the event description.

When cancelling a recurring booking with multiple calendar references, the recurring-event deletion over all remaining bookings and credentials runs once per reference, causing duplicate delete calls and errors.

findings.description: Team admins are incorrectly denied permission to add booking guests — Requiring `isTeamOwner` excludes ADMIN members who are neither the organizer nor an attendee, since it accepts only OWNER memberships. Use `isTeamAdmin` alone because it already accepts both ADMIN and OWNER memberships.

Case-sensitive guest checks allow blocked email addresses — An authorized attendee can bypass `blacklistedGuestEmails` by changing an address’s letter case. Normalize `guests` before filtering and persisting them, and normalize `attendee.email` for comparison.

Guest additions use requester credentials for organizer calendar updates — Calendar updates can fail when someone other than the organizer adds guests: for references without `credentialId`, `EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents` selects the requester’s credentials by type. Initialize `EventManager` with `booking.user` and their credentials, rejecting bookings without an organizer.

Guest filtering allows duplicate attendees and repeated invitations — Repeated addresses in `uniqueGuests` can create duplicate attendee rows and invitations; check the server schema and `Attendee` model for missing uniqueness enforcement. Deduplicate normalized addresses before constructing `guestsFullDetails`, and enforce booking/address uniqueness to cover concurrent requests.

goldensDetail.text: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, so only team owners pass; team admins who are not organizer or attendee are wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN.

The guest blacklist is lowercased but incoming guest emails are compared without normalization, so a blacklisted address submitted with different casing bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and is added and emailed.
The server never deduplicates the guests array, so a request with the same email twice inserts duplicate attendee rows for the booking.

The handler passes the unfiltered guests list to sendAddGuestsEmails, which uses it to pick who gets AttendeeScheduledEmail, so existing attendees included in the request receive a new-booking confirmation instead of the add-guests email.

EventManager is created with the requesting user's credentials, so when a non-organizer adds guests the organizer's calendar event is not updated (or the wrong account is used) for references without a credentialId.
sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings, so hosts and attendees receive add-guests emails even when standard emails are disabled.

The add-guests handler omits booking.iCalUID from the CalendarEvent, so the add-guests emails' .ics attachments use booking.uid as UID and recipients' calendars treat them as a new event rather than an update of the original booking invite.
Guest email uniqueness is checked case-sensitively, so case variants of the same address are accepted as distinct guests (and slip past the lowercased blacklist).

findings.description: Synchronized OAuth refresh returns a raw Response instead of token data — Google and Zoho/Bigin consumers expect `.data`, while HubSpot expects decoded token fields, so returning `response` breaks successful refreshes when synchronization is enabled. Decode it in `refreshOAuthTokens` and adapt it to each consumer, or normalize both branches and update all consumers.

Refreshed credentials are stored as a safe-parse result instead of token fields — Saving `key` persists the safe-parse wrapper from `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, so subsequent `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` calls cannot load the refreshed credentials. Check `key.success`, throw `key.error` on failure, and persist `key.data`.

OAuth refresh uses credential ID instead of user ID — Passing `credentialId` as `calcomUserId` makes the sync endpoint look up the wrong user's credentials or reject the request. Pass `credential.userId` from `biginAuth` separately, retaining `credentialId` for database updates.

Salesforce initialization references an unimported Prisma client — The unresolved `prisma` reference prevents compilation or fails at runtime during Salesforce initialization if transpilation proceeds. Import `prisma` from `@calcom/prisma` before calling `prisma.credential.update`.

Computed schema keys strip real expiry fields from token responses — Zoom and Office365 lose required expiry values because `z.string().toString()` creates a literal schema key rather than matching fields such as `expires_in`. Define supported expiry fields explicitly or preserve and validate additional fields in `parseRefreshTokenResponse`.

Concurrent webhook deliveries can create duplicate app credentials — Concurrent deliveries can both find no matching credential and call `prisma.credential.create`, producing duplicate rows because `Credential` lacks a user/app uniqueness constraint. Serialize the operation per user/app, or enforce that uniqueness in `Credential` and use an atomic upsert.

Salesforce client construction refreshes tokens and writes credentials unconditionally — The unconditional token `fetch` and `prisma.credential.update` add an external round trip and database write before every Salesforce service operation, even when the token remains valid. Preserve jsforce's on-demand refresh behavior or refresh only when the current token needs replacement.

goldensDetail.text: The webhook parses the body with zod .parse and decrypts/JSON-parses the keys without error handling, so invalid payloads produce 500 errors instead of 400 responses.
parseRefreshTokenResponse writes the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when the refresh response omits a refresh token, so the stored credential gets an invalid refresh token and later refreshes fail.

minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys from z.string().toString(), which produce a literal key rather than a wildcard, so the sync-mode schema does not validate or keep expiry and other token fields as intended.
Google Calendar persists the safeParse result object instead of its data as the credential key, corrupting the stored credential so later reads fail.
Salesforce getClient now refreshes the OAuth token and writes the credential on every service construction, adding a network round trip and DB write even when the access token is valid.
The new Salesforce token refresh uses prisma without importing it, so the code fails type checking and throws a ReferenceError at runtime.
Salesforce checks response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok when refreshing the token, which can misclassify successful responses, and then ignores the refreshed token.
After refreshing the Salesforce token, jsforce.Connection is created with the stale access_token and instance_url instead of the newly refreshed values.

The app-credential webhook looks up appStoreMetadata by app.slug, but the map is keyed by dirName, so apps whose slug differs from their directory (e.g. google-calendar) always get a 404 and their credentials cannot be synced.

findings.description: Retry persistence errors abort scheduling for the remaining SMS reminders — If cancellation deletes a loaded reminder, `prisma.workflowReminder.update` throws and skips the remaining batch. Use `prisma.workflowReminder.updateMany` filtered by `id` with an atomic `retryCount` increment so deletion is a no-op, and catch persistence errors within the per-reminder handler.

goldensDetail.text: retryCount is set to reminder.retryCount + 1 from a value read at the start of the run instead of an atomic increment, so overlapping runs can lose increments.
The deleteMany OR clause applies retryCount > 1 without the SMS method filter, so the SMS cron deletes any workflow reminder (email, WhatsApp) with retryCount above 1.

The retry-count update inside the catch block is not guarded, so if it throws (for example the reminder was deleted concurrently) the error escapes the loop and the cron run fails, skipping the remaining reminders.
Claims transient errors increment retryCount, so two runs during an outage delete the whole pending SMS reminder queue.

SMS-sending locks are counted as failed scheduling attempts: scheduleSMS returns undefined for locked users/teams, retryCount is incremented, and after two cron runs the retryCount > 1 cleanup deletes future reminders even if sending is later unlocked.

findings.description: Backup-code login bypasses password verification when TOTP is supplied — A stolen `backupCode` can authenticate without the account password because any nonempty `totpCode` skips the preceding password guards. Require password verification for `IdentityProvider.CAL` backup-code authentication regardless of whether `totpCode` is supplied.

Concurrent backup-code logins allow reuse and restore consumed codes — Unconditional writes through `prisma.user.update` break the one-time guarantee of `backupCodes` when requests validate the same stored list. Atomically compare and replace `user.backupCodes`, rejecting or retrying requests whose conditional update affects no rows.

Dismissing backup codes leaves the 2FA settings switch disabled — After successful setup, Escape or an outside click leaves `viewer.me` stale because only the Close button invokes `onEnable`. Handle dismissal of `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes` by resetting local state and invoking `onEnable` too.

goldensDetail.text: The credentials authorize() skips the password check when any totpCode is present, and the new backup-code branch never validates that totpCode, so a backup code plus a dummy totpCode logs in without the account password.
The getBaseConditions test uses a single booking matching both auth and filter conditions, so it would pass even if the conditions were not combined.
The new public options type makes teamId optional for team scope, so a missing teamId compiles and silently yields empty insights instead of a type error.
Claims getBaseConditions returns OR fragments without parentheses, so a caller appending `AND <extra>` would leak rows outside the authorization scope.

findings.description: Unsanitized feed HTML enables stored XSS in embedded posts — Feed HTML passed to `PostCreator.new` with `Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` renders unsanitized on the forum origin, enabling stored XSS. Sanitize imported HTML using the forum's safe HTML policy before storing or rendering it.

Feed entries without content crash polling and block subsequent imports — Description-only entries have no `i.content`, so calling `scrub` raises and blocks subsequent imports. Fall back to `i.description`, then an empty string, before calling `scrub`.
Incomplete Ruby conditional causes an embed template syntax error — Rendering an existing embedded topic fails because `end if` leaves an incomplete Ruby modifier conditional. Replace it with `end`.

Link and image URLs are resolved incorrectly against the source article — In `absolutize_urls`, protocol-relative references become paths on the article host, while document-relative references resolve against the forum. Resolve `href` and `src` against `url` with `URI.join` instead of concatenating `prefix`.

Uncached article requests each synchronously poll the entire feed — Calling `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute` for each uncached article multiplies feed downloads and per-entry database work during simultaneous first visits. Share polling throttling or caching across article URLs and worker processes, and reuse the latest feed results.

goldensDetail.text: The referer and embed_url host checks compare against SiteSetting.embeddable_host case-sensitively, so a host differing only in case is rejected even though hostnames are case-insensitive.

PollFeed reads i.content.scrub for every feed item, so items without a content element (common in RSS feeds that only have description) raise NoMethodError and abort the import of the remaining items.

TopicEmbed.import appends a footer that interpolates the URL unescaped into an <a href='...'> tag in raw HTML that is later rendered unsanitized, so a crafted URL can inject markup; it also appends to contents with << without handling nil.
When the embedded post has been deleted, TopicEmbed.import's update path passes a nil embed.post to PostRevisor and crashes on every later import of that URL.
Claims import_remote crashes on unparseable pages (nil content) and dead URLs because it does no nil check or network error handling around open(url).read.

absolutize_urls only handles root-relative paths: protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/x.png are rewritten to http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png and path-relative links are left unresolved, breaking links and images in imported posts.

Every retrieval of an article not yet embedded synchronously polls and imports the entire RSS feed, and since throttling is per URL, many different article requests repeat the full feed download and processing.

The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' specs leave feed_polling_enabled at its false default, so they never reach the condition they name and would pass with those checks deleted.
`import_remote` fetches the embed URL with open-uri, which follows redirects, so the embeddable-host check on the initial URL can be bypassed to reach internal services (SSRF).
The retrieve throttle is keyed by the full embed URL, so an anonymous client can vary the query string on the embeddable host to bypass it and make the server create an unbounded number of topics.

The "requires feed_polling_enabled?" spec leaves feed_polling_url and embed_by_username at their blank defaults, so poll_feed is skipped regardless and the test would pass even without the enabled check.
The embed layout references the 'embed' stylesheet and embed.js, but neither is in config.assets.precompile, so with precompiled assets in production the embed page fails to load them.

findings.description: Missing embed category causes migration to fail before fallback — Upgrades without a configured `embed_category` raise an exception because `execute(...)[0]['id']` dereferences a missing row before the fallback runs. Check whether the first row exists before reading its ID, and use the uncategorized fallback when it does not.

Migrated host URLs retain schemes and paths that prevent host matching — Legacy entries such as `https://example.com` stop matching because `record_for_host` compares stored values against `URI(url).host`. Strip schemes and paths from `h` before insertion, matching the normalization in `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`.

Host validation rejects valid TLDs longer than five letters — Administrators cannot configure embedding for valid domains such as `example.museum` and `example.technology`, which the previous setting accepted. Remove the five-character TLD limit from the `host` validation.

goldensDetail.text: The migration reads execute(...)[0]['id'] for embed_category without checking for an empty result, so installs without that setting stored crash the migration instead of falling back to the uncategorized category.

After saving a host, the component overwrites its category with findById(categoryId); when no category was chosen this is null even though the server saved the uncategorized category, so the row shows no category until reload.
Hosts saved with a port (allowed by the validation regex) are stored as host:port, but lookup compares only URI.host, so those configured hosts never match and embedding fails for them.
EmbeddableHost's host format validation only accepts TLDs of 2-5 letters, so admins cannot add embeddable hosts on longer TLDs like example.technology.

findings.description: Header extra-info flex item cannot shrink around long topic titles — Long, nonwrapping topic titles can push navigation outside the header because the `header-extra-info` outer div retains `min-width: auto` inside `.contents`. Apply `min-width: 0` and let that flex item consume remaining width; the existing `overflow: hidden` on `.extra-info-wrapper` only affects the nested child.

goldensDetail.text: The flex-item styles target the inner .extra-info-wrapper instead of the component's root div, so in the flexbox header a long topic title keeps its full width and pushes the navigation panel out instead of being truncated.
The align-items mixin emits no -moz-box-align, so on old Firefox versions using the display:-moz-box fallback the advertised vertical centering is not applied.

Removing the float-based right alignment of .d-header .panel leaves the server-rendered (no-JS) header's login panel, which sits inside .row and is not a flex item, no longer right-aligned next to the title.

Making .small-action a flex container leaves .small-action-desc content-sized (no flex:1), so the right-floated edit/delete buttons inside it sit right after short action descriptions instead of at the right edge of the row.

On mobile the .small-action custom message keeps margin-left:-40px, tuned for the old 4em left padding; with the new flex layout and 1.5% padding it is pulled into the avatar column and overlaps the icon.

findings.description: Duplicate downsize definition breaks width-and-height callers — `Jobs::ResizeEmoji.execute` raises `ArgumentError` when passing five arguments because the second `downsize` definition replaces the width-and-height version. Keep one `downsize` method supporting both argument forms, or give the geometry-based method a distinct name.

Unconditional 10 MB ceiling overrides configured attachment size limit — Attachments larger than 10 MB are rejected even when `max_attachment_size_kb` permits them. Apply the preprocessing ceiling in `maxSizeKB` only to images and retain the configured limit for attachments.

Oversized multipart GIF uploads lose animation during downsizing — Animation is lost despite `allow_animated_thumbnails` because `OptimizedImage.optimize` checks the temporary path’s `.gif` suffix rather than `filename`, otherwise invoking `convert` with `[0]`. Preserve the original extension in a processing tempfile or pass the image format explicitly to animation dispatch.

goldensDetail.text: downsize is defined twice in OptimizedImage; the new (from, to, dimensions, opts) version overrides the (max_width, max_height) one, so existing callers such as ResizeEmoji that pass width and height now raise ArgumentError.

The client-side upload size check hardcodes 10 MB instead of the per-type max_<type>_size_kb setting, so attachment limits diverge from the server: larger allowed attachments are blocked and smaller limits are only enforced server-side.
The upload downsizing passes a percentage ('80%') as dimensions, but for animated GIFs the gifsicle path uses --resize-fit, which expects WxH geometry, so downsizing silently fails.
Auto-downsizing passes the upload tempfile path, which lacks a .gif extension, so the animated branch is never chosen and convert keeps only the first frame, flattening oversized animated GIFs.
Claims the downsize loop checking tempfile.size may never terminate because of a stale cached size, causing infinite loops.
Oversized SVG uploads go through the new ImageMagick downsize loop because SVG counts as an image, so the vector file is rasterized or corrupted in place before Upload.create_for parses it as SVG.

The upload tempfile path, which for API URL uploads embeds the request-controlled type param, is now passed to OptimizedImage.downsize and run unescaped in a shell via backticks, allowing command injection through type.
The 413 upload error message states a hard-coded 10 MB maximum that may not match the limit the server or web server actually enforces.

findings.description: Public group members page hides members beyond the first 50 — Members beyond the first 50 become inaccessible because `findMembers` loads one page and `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` has no pagination controls. Add public pagination or incremental loading.

Page count adds an empty page at exact multiples of the member limit — At every positive multiple of `limit`, `totalPages` enables Next to fetch an empty page. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` to count pages.

Removing a member leaves their primary group reference intact — Post serialization can still display the removed group because `group.users.delete(user_id)` leaves `primary_group_id` intact; check the previous cleanup in `Group#destroy_deletions`. Clear the removed user's matching `primary_group_id` in the same transaction as the membership deletion.

goldensDetail.text: The admin group pager computes total pages as floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so when the member count is an exact multiple of the limit it shows an extra page and Next navigates to an empty member list.
Paging actions fire overlapping member requests and each response unconditionally overwrites offset and members, so a stale response arriving last can revert the list to an earlier page.
The public members endpoint now always caps results at 50 per page, but the public group members page has no pagination, so groups with more than 50 members are silently truncated for users.
Creating a group ignores the alias_level the admin selected, saving only name and visibility, so new groups keep the default alias level.
Removing a member deletes the membership row directly and skips clearing the user's primary_group_id, so a removed user can keep this group as their primary group.
Group member pagination is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit: Next moves to offset == user_count and shows an empty page.
Admin remove_member deletes memberships with group.users.delete, which skips GroupUser callbacks, so the cached groups.user_count is never decremented and stays inflated.

Admin add_members pushes every username into group.users without skipping existing members, so adding someone already in the group hits the unique group_users index, returns a 500 and leaves earlier users partially added.
The public group members endpoint takes `limit` from params with no upper bound or positivity check, letting a visitor request huge pages or trigger a 500 with a negative limit.
Admin remove_member calls group.users.delete with a raw integer id, which raises RecordNotFound (404/500) when the user is not or no longer a member, e.g. on concurrent removal.

findings.description: Translation cache ignores the site's fallback locale — Sites sharing a process can receive another site's fallback language, and changing `SiteSetting.default_locale` leaves cached translations stale. Include `SiteSetting.default_locale` in the accelerator cache key; check the accelerator's cache-key implementation.

goldensDetail.text: Fallback locale catalogs are only loaded in the controller's set_locale filter, while translate loads just the current locale, so translations outside requests (jobs, mailers) cannot fall back to the site default or English.

The translation cache key does not include the site or its default locale, but fallback results now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, so multisite processes or a changed default locale serve stale fallback translations.

findings.description: Rejected devices bypass the admission limit on subsequent requests — A rejected device authenticates on retry because `tagDeviceUI` populates `localCache` before `CreateOrUpdateDevice` fails, and cache hits skip admission checks; check `tagDeviceUI` in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl`. Cache devices only after successful persistence, and never treat rejected devices as admitted.

Concurrent device admissions can exceed the configured limit — Concurrent requests can each observe a count below `deviceLimit` through `CountDevices` and then insert because counting and insertion use separate sessions without serialization. Make admission atomic across server instances with a database lock or equivalent mechanism around the count-and-write operation.

Missing device header bypasses anonymous device limit — Anonymous callers can gain access at capacity by omitting `X-Grafana-Device-Id`: `TagDevice` returns nil without it, so `Authenticate` grants access; check `TagDevice` in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl`. Enforce admission for requests without a device identifier rather than relying on an optional client-supplied header.

goldensDetail.text: tagDeviceUI caches the device key before CreateOrUpdateDevice; when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the entry stays, so the next request from the same device skips the limit check and authenticates for up to 29 minutes.
The new auth.anonymous device_limit setting has no entry in conf/defaults.ini, so the GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT environment override is ignored and the limit stays 0.

findings.description: Request cancellation can abort background legacy writes — Returning the response can cancel replication before it finishes because `context.WithTimeoutCause` inherits request cancellation. Derive background timeouts from `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` in `Create`, `Update`, `Delete`, and `DeleteCollection` to preserve request values without inheriting cancellation.

Legacy updates replay patches against potentially stale objects — Passing `objInfo` to `d.Legacy.Update` recomputes patches against potentially stale legacy data, which can produce divergent records or fail during replay. Pass an `updateWrapper` containing `res` to persist the successful unified result.

Resource names in delete histogram labels cause unbounded cardinality — Each distinct `name` creates a permanently retained histogram series, increasing metric memory use and scrape cardinality with deletion history. Pass `options.Kind` instead of `name` to `d.recordStorageDuration`.

Unified Create and Update failures are attributed to legacy storage — Calling `d.recordLegacyDuration` when legacy storage was never called hides unified errors and inflates legacy error metrics. Use `d.recordStorageDuration` for the unified failure paths in both `Create` and `Update`.

Legacy DeleteCollection metrics are attributed to unified storage — Calling `d.recordStorageDuration` for legacy completion double-counts unified operations and assigns legacy failures to the wrong backend. Use `d.recordLegacyDuration` for the legacy `DeleteCollection` result.

goldensDetail.text: The legacy DeleteCollection goroutine records its duration with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, misattributing legacy latency and errors to the storage metric.
Delete's success path records the storage metric with the object name in the kind label instead of options.Kind, creating per-object series and inconsistent labels.
On storage Create/Update failure the duration is recorded with recordLegacyDuration, attributing unified-store errors to the legacy metric.

Mode 3 legacy writes now run in background goroutines derived from the request context, which is cancelled when the request completes, so legacy writes can be cancelled and legacy storage falls out of sync.
Legacy.Update now receives the original objInfo instead of a wrapper carrying the object stored in unified storage, so legacy recomputes the update and can diverge.
The Mode 3 tests never wait for or assert the asynchronous legacy writes, and legacy and storage share one mock, so removing the legacy calls would not fail them.
Independent per-request goroutines remove ordering between legacy writes to the same resource, so legacy can end up with an older version or a resurrected object.
Mode 3 legacy-storage write errors (create/update/delete/delete-collection) are no longer logged after moving to async goroutines; only a duration metric with an error flag is recorded.
DualWriterMode3.Delete now returns on any unified-storage error, including NotFound, before deleting from legacy, so objects that exist only in legacy can no longer be deleted.

findings.description: Concurrent builds can overwrite cached indexes and lose event updates — A cache miss from `GetIndex` during construction can create competing indexes, losing event updates when one replaces another. Serialize construction per key and recheck the cache after acquiring that key’s lock, while allowing different keys to build concurrently.

Startup document counting races with concurrent index creation — An event can publish an index while `TotalDocs` traverses the cache, triggering a fatal concurrent map iteration/write. Protect traversal in `bleveBackend.TotalDocs` with `cacheMu.RLock` or take a protected snapshot before counting documents.

goldensDetail.text: BuildIndex now locks only the final cache assignment, so concurrent callers for the same uncached key all build the same expensive index in parallel and the last one overwrites the others.

The new startup log calls TotalDocs, which iterates the index cache without a lock, after the event goroutine that can add indexes has started, so a concurrent map read and write can crash the process.
The PR skips the storage-server module integration test on postgres instead of fixing the failure, removing coverage of the new eager initialization on postgres.

findings.description: Grafana rules lose Pause and Delete actions without rulerRule — Update those menu items and their handlers to use the Prometheus rule identifier before removing the `rulerRule` input.

Silence notifications action does not open for Prometheus-only rules — Clicking Silence notifications only sets `showSilenceDrawer`; the drawer's `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` guard fails when `rule` is undefined. Update the drawer wiring to accept the Prometheus rule UID so the action opens the editor.

CombinedRule abilities no longer enforce federated-group immutability — Existing `useAlertRuleAbility` consumers can now enable editing federated Mimir rules because `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` hardcodes `isFederated` to false. Preserve the group-level federation restriction when adapting `CombinedRule` abilities.

Skipped Grafana rule abilities incorrectly enable datasource duplication — `AlertRuleMenu` combines Grafana and datasource abilities, so `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` granting Duplicate for an absent rule exposes the action even when datasource duplication is unsupported or denied. Return disabled abilities when `rule` is `skipToken`.

goldensDetail.text: The pause menu item is still gated on a Grafana ruler rule, but the list view now passes only the Prometheus rule, so Pause/Resume disappears for list-view rules even when the user may pause them.
The Delete menu item still requires a ruler rule, which list-view Grafana rules no longer provide, so users with delete permission lose the Delete action.

When the Grafana prom-rule branch is skipped (datasource rules), useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) still reports Duplicate as supported and allowed by Grafana create permission, and AlertRuleMenu ORs it with the ruler ability, so Duplicate appears on cloud rules even when the ruler check denies it.

For list-view Grafana rules RuleActionsButtons gets only promRule, so the Silence menu item is shown but the silence drawer, still gated on a ruler alerting rule, never renders and clicking Silence does nothing.

findings.description: Access token ID matcher accepts incorrect grant types — The four event assertions accept incorrect grant types because `substring(3, 5)` checks the wrong offsets and equality triggers rejection. Require a six-character prefix and reject when `substring(4, 6)` differs from `expectedGrantShortcut`.

Grant shortcut contract recommends a length rejected by token ID decoding — Custom grants following `getShortcut`'s three-letter recommendation mint IDs that `getTokenContextFromTokenId` rejects because it requires a two-character grant in a six-character prefix. Specify exactly two characters and validate shortcut length during factory initialization before issuing tokens.

Nonstandard token exchanges omit the grant type from access token IDs — V1, federated, and impersonation exchanges through `AbstractTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient` still encode `na` in access token IDs because their grant attribute is unset. Set `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` to `OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE` on the shared path's client session context before generating the access token.

Exception assertion can pass before the reader thread finishes — An in-flight groups request can append an exception to `caughtExceptions` after the test has passed. Keep the reader thread reference and join it after setting `deletedAll` and before asserting `caughtExceptions`.

Overlapping prefix and suffix trimming crashes HTML validation — Sanitizing `x` makes `start` exceed `sanitized.length() - end`, causing `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` and aborting diagnostic aggregation. Bound `end` by each string’s remaining length after `start` so malformed translations produce validation messages instead.

Choice normalization hides attacker-controlled HTML from validation — Replacing entire choice expressions in `value` removes branch text before anchor validation and HTML sanitization, letting attacker-selected links pass unchecked. Change `value.replaceAll` to mask only the `ChoiceFormat` comparison syntax while preserving branch text for validation.

Lithuanian OTP enrollment instructions appear in Italian in both bundles — Lithuanian users receive Italian OTP enrollment instructions from `loginTotpStep1` and the account bundle’s `totpStep1`. Replace both values with Lithuanian translations of the new instruction.

goldensDetail.text: The diff-trimming code computes common prefix and suffix independently, so they can overlap and substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the verifier instead of reporting the illegal HTML.

The account and admin UI bundles now use Java MessageFormat placeholders and choice syntax for error-invalid-multivalued-size, but i18next expects {{n}}, so the UI shows literal {0}/{1}/{2} and the raw choice text.

findings.description: All-clients view grant bypasses client-specific policy denial — Delegated administrators can read explicitly excluded clients through `ClientResource.getClient` because `canView(client)` returns before checking client-specific denials. Replace `canView()` with `canViewClientDefault()` so client-specific policies are evaluated before falling back to all-clients permissions.

Type-filtered lookup omits individually authorized client resources — `AvailableRoleMappingResource` cannot discover individually authorized clients because `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` creates their resources without the type required by `resourceStore.findByType`. Assign `AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE` when creating individual client resources.

goldensDetail.text: Claims the removal-cleanup listener is guarded by the V1 fine-grained flag, so client/role/group permissions are orphaned when V1 is disabled or only V2 is enabled.

getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 only finds the type-level 'Clients' resource and returns its name, never actual client ids, so callers that resolve the returned values as client ids get wrong results or null clients.
Claims getResourceTypeResource can return null in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, causing a NullPointerException in findByResource.
ClientPermissionsV2.canView() ignores a global MANAGE permission, so admins with only global manage take the unpaginated, per-client evaluated listing path.
canView(client) short-circuits on the global all-clients VIEW permission, so a client-specific permission denying an admin is never evaluated and the client is still viewable.

The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, an admin granted a permission on all clients is denied on any client that also has its own per-client permission resource, because only the per-client resource is evaluated.

ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AbstractTokenExchangeProvider still calls clients().canExchangeTo for client-to-client exchange, so with token exchange and FGAP V2 enabled the request fails with a server error instead of a permission decision.

findings.description: Passkey-only users cannot authenticate with the legacy keycloak theme — Users admitted by `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user)` cannot complete authentication with the legacy `keycloak` theme because `base/login/login-password.ftl` lacks WebAuthn controls. Add the passkey macro to that template as well as `keycloak.v2`.

Organization-aware state leaves hidden providers in the login cache — A provider hidden while its organization is disabled can reappear after re-enabling because `original` is organization-aware but `updated` is raw. Reload `original` through `idpDelegate.getById()` before evaluating `getLoginPredicate()` so cache invalidation compares persisted models.

goldensDetail.text: The test registers cleanup for the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases, so the created identity providers are never cleaned up.

Adding the organization/BROKER_PUBLIC check to the shared LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate also changes IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate, so with organizations disabled a user's linked IdP that has an organizationId but is not public is no longer shown on the login page.

findings.description: Enabled table visualization renders empty columns and rows — Organizations with `use-table-widget-visualization` enabled see empty dashboard tables even when `tableResults` contains results. Populate `tableData` with the current result's data and metadata, and derive `columns` from the widget fields instead of using empty placeholders.

Attribute query cache is shared across organizations — Switching organizations with identical project and date selections reuses cached attributes from the previous organization, although `useGetTraceItemAttributeKeys` fetches from an organization-specific endpoint. Include the organization slug in `queryKey` to isolate cached results and in-flight requests.

Truthy checks allow mutually exclusive age and timestamp fields — Reports containing both `age: 0` and `timestamp: 0` pass validation despite the exclusivity contract. In `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age`, check key membership in `self.initial_data` instead of value truthiness.

goldensDetail.text: The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators check truthiness via initial_data.get(), so a zero value is treated as absent and a report carrying both fields passes validation.
The validation-failure warning logs the entire raw, attacker-controlled browser report instead of a redacted subset.
The Snuba replay lookup for error IDs runs even when enable_error_context=false, adding a needless query (and failure point) to opt-out requests.

With the use-table-widget-visualization flag on, the widget renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded empty columns and data instead of the query results, so every table widget shows an empty table.
The custom cell renderers fall back to default rendering on any falsy return (0, '', null), not only undefined, so a renderer cannot render zero or an empty cell.
The attribute-keys query key no longer includes the organization slug, so two organizations with the same filters share a cache entry and switching orgs can show the previous org's attribute names.

Every paginated breadcrumb-summary request queries the replay and fetches all of its error events from nodestore with no cap, adding latency and memory proportional to the replay's error count on each page.
HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES is applied only when a search query is present; the no-search early return shows all attributes, so the hidden attributes still appear in the default span attributes view.

The bulk delete test sets max_segment_id to None to cover the new guard in _make_recording_filenames, but it mocks delete_matched_rows, so the guard is never executed and removing it would not fail the test.
Error event timestamps (seconds) are compared with replay recording event timestamps (milliseconds), so errors are not interleaved chronologically with breadcrumbs.

findings.description: Process type guard skips killing hung spawn-context workers — A hung `SpawnProcess` can survive replacement and flush the same shards concurrently because it fails the `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` check. Check against `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` so workers created by `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process` also receive `kill()`.

Expired join deadline skips termination of remaining workers — Workers blocked in Redis or Kafka can remain alive after shutdown or rebalancing, including every worker if `next_step.join(timeout)` exhausts the budget. When `remaining_time` reaches zero, stop waiting but still run termination cleanup for every worker.

Memory backpressure repeats cluster-wide Redis queries for every worker — With memory backpressure enabled, each submit synchronously repeats cluster-wide Redis requests because `buffer.get_memory_info()` calls `iter_cluster_memory_usage`, which queries all shards regardless of buffer assignments. Query memory through a single buffer instead of every buffer in `self.buffers`.

goldensDetail.text: The restart path only kills a hung flusher if it is a multiprocessing.Process, but spawn-context workers are SpawnProcess, so hung processes are never killed and a duplicate flusher is started for the same shards.
join() breaks out of the per-process loop when the shared deadline expires, skipping termination of the remaining flusher processes and leaving them running after shutdown.

findings.description: AssignmentSource reuses the import-time timestamp for every instance — Assignments without an explicit `queued` value report the process import time, and `to_dict()` propagates that incorrect timestamp. Use `dataclasses.field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each `AssignmentSource` gets its own queue timestamp.

Reconnection crashes when existing integrations lack sender metadata — Normal setup can omit sender metadata, causing `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` to raise `KeyError`; check `build_integration` and pipeline completion. Handle missing metadata explicitly and verify installation ownership before allowing reconnection.

Missing integration rows bypass GitHub installer ownership validation — A delayed or missing installation webhook lets `Integration.DoesNotExist` bypass ownership validation because `build_integration` accepts valid installation IDs using app credentials. Require verified installer information matching `github_authenticated_user` before completing that branch too.

Predictable OAuth state allows GitHub login CSRF — Every user receives the same state because `pipeline.signature` hashes view class names deterministically; check `Pipeline.__init__`. Generate an unpredictable nonce per pipeline session, persist it in pipeline state, and validate and consume it on callback instead of using `pipeline.signature`.

goldensDetail.text: test_installation_not_found uses a wrong OAuth state, so it fails at the state check and never reaches the installation-not-found path it is meant to test.

findings.description: Metric alert handler is abstract and fails during instantiation — `Detector.detector_handler` raises `TypeError` when instantiating `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` for `metric_alert_fire`, aborting processing before evaluation. Implement the abstract members required by `StatefulDetectorHandler`, or retain a concrete no-op `DetectorHandler` until the stateful implementation is available.

goldensDetail.text: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing its abstract methods, so instantiating it for metric alert detectors raises TypeError where it previously returned an empty-result handler.

The mock occurrence builder ignores its value argument, so tests (e.g. group_2 expected with 6 while the packet carries 10) pass regardless of which value is passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data.

findings.description: Undefined credential passed to updateEvent aborts remaining calendar updates — An undefined `credential` reaches `updateEvent` and throws a TypeError, aborting updates for all remaining calendar references. Skip the reference or push a failure result when `credential` is not found.
Team destination calendars dropped when no event type or organizer calendar exists — Initialize it as `[]` instead of `null`.

createEvent omits destination.externalId when destination has no credentialId — Without `destination.externalId`, the saved reference has an undefined `externalCalendarId`, so reschedule and cancel lose the target calendar and Google falls back to "primary". Pass `destination.externalId` as the third argument to `createEvent`, and have the calendar services select by `externalId` when no `credentialId` matches.
TypeError on Google Meet booking when destinationCalendar is empty — Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration` so it falls back to Cal Video.

Calendar ID fallback in updateEvent can never match and yields undefined — The fallback `find` only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it never matches and `selectedCalendar` is undefined, sending `events.update` and `events.patch` without a `calendarId`. Fall back to `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId` or "primary" instead.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:315-317`

Video booking references lose credentialId for non-calendar results — Video booking references no longer store their credential, so later reschedule and cancel flows that look it up by `credentialId` must guess. Keep `credentialId: result.credentialId` for non-calendar types.

events.patch uses undefined calendarId when no destination calendar matches — The later `events.patch` call still passes the raw `selectedCalendar`, which is often undefined now that `events.insert` falls back to "primary", so the Meet link patch fails or hits the wrong calendar. Compute `selectedCalendar` once with the "primary" fallback and use it in both calls.

Recurring calendar deletion runs once per reference inside loop — With N calendar references, the remaining bookings' events are deleted N times per credential, causing duplicate API calls and spurious errors. Move the recurring deletion outside the loop and keep only the non-recurring path per reference.

Raw Prisma error message leaked to client in loadUsers catch block — Prisma messages expose query and schema details, and `loadUsers` returns them to the booking client in a 400. Log the original error server-side and throw a generic "Unable to load users" instead.

Slug is set only when team billing is enabled, inverting original condition — The inverted condition sets `slug` only when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`, the opposite of the original behavior. Restore the negation with `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`.

goldensDetail.text: When externalCalendarId is absent, updateEvent/deleteEvent look for a destination calendar whose externalId equals that absent value, so the lookup never matches and the configured destination calendar is no longer used.
The organization slug is now set only when team billing is enabled (inverted condition), so with billing both slug and requestedSlug are set and without billing neither is.

Office365 (and Lark) createEvent ignore the new credentialId argument and always use the first destination calendar, so in collective bookings other hosts' credentials target the organizer's calendar instead of their own.

The Google Meet fallback reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining, so a Meet booking with a null or empty destinationCalendar throws instead of falling back to Cal Video.

For collective events whose organizer has no destination calendar, destinationCalendar is null and the optional push drops all other hosts' destination calendars, so those hosts never get calendar events.
Video booking references are now saved without their credentialId, so cancelling the booking can no longer find the video credential and the meeting is not deleted.

Cancelling all remaining occurrences of a recurring collective booking deletes only the first calendar reference of each booking, repeated once per host, so the other hosts' events stay on their calendars.

In Google createEvent, when no destination calendar matches the credentialId, the hangout-link events.patch is called with an undefined calendarId and fails, so the Meet link is not added to the event description.

When cancelling a recurring booking with multiple calendar references, the recurring-event deletion over all remaining bookings and credentials runs once per reference, causing duplicate delete calls and errors.

findings.description: `EventManager` uses the requesting user's credentials, not the organizer's — Calendar updates run against the wrong credentials, so `updateCalendarAttendees` does not update the organizer's event when an attendee or team admin adds guests. Build `EventManager` from `booking.user` and its credentials, as the other booking handlers do.

`isTeamAdminOrOwner` joins `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` with `&&` — `isTeamAdmin` already matches admins and owners, so joining it with `isTeamOwner` using `&&` limits access to owners and returns FORBIDDEN for other team admins. Use `isTeamAdmin` alone or join the checks with `||`, and skip the lookup when `teamId` is null.

Blacklisted guest emails bypass filter when entered with upper-case letters — The blacklist is lowercased but `guest` is compared as typed, so a blacklisted address with upper-case letters gets through. Compare `guest.toLowerCase()` against `blacklistedGuestEmails`.

Unbounded guests array allows mass email sending in one request — One authenticated call can add arbitrarily many attendees, and `sendAddGuestsEmails` emails every attendee, the organizer and each team member, so work grows with guests × attendees. Add `.min(1)` and `.max(N)` to the `guests` array.

Error toast always shows raw error code prefix; fallback message is unreachable — The message is always a truthy string, so the `t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback never runs and users see a raw prefix such as "FORBIDDEN:". Show the translated `err.message`, falling back to `t("unable_to_add_guests")` when it is empty.

Duplicate guest emails in input are not deduplicated before createMany — Uniqueness is enforced only in the client dialog, so a direct API call with repeated emails makes `createMany` insert duplicate attendee rows. Dedupe `guests` before filtering, and compare against the lowercased `blacklistedGuestEmails`.

sendAddGuestsEmails receives unfiltered guests instead of uniqueGuests — Duplicate and blacklisted emails still match `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`, so existing attendees get a full scheduled-invite email instead of the add-guests notice. Pass `uniqueGuests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails` instead of `guests`.

Case-sensitive guest email checks allow duplicate or blacklisted guests — The `guest === attendee.email` check is case-sensitive, so a case variant of an existing attendee's email counts as a new guest and creates a duplicate. Compare lowercased values in the `uniqueGuests` filter, and dedupe submitted guests case-insensitively too.

goldensDetail.text: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, so only team owners pass; team admins who are not organizer or attendee are wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN.

The guest blacklist is lowercased but incoming guest emails are compared without normalization, so a blacklisted address submitted with different casing bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and is added and emailed.
The server never deduplicates the guests array, so a request with the same email twice inserts duplicate attendee rows for the booking.

The handler passes the unfiltered guests list to sendAddGuestsEmails, which uses it to pick who gets AttendeeScheduledEmail, so existing attendees included in the request receive a new-booking confirmation instead of the add-guests email.

EventManager is created with the requesting user's credentials, so when a non-organizer adds guests the organizer's calendar event is not updated (or the wrong account is used) for references without a credentialId.
sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings, so hosts and attendees receive add-guests emails even when standard emails are disabled.

The add-guests handler omits booking.iCalUID from the CalendarEvent, so the add-guests emails' .ics attachments use booking.uid as UID and recipients' calendars treat them as a new event rather than an update of the original booking invite.
Guest email uniqueness is checked case-sensitively, so case variants of the same address are accepted as distinct guests (and slip past the lowercased blacklist).

findings.description: Placeholder refresh_token applied outside credential sync mode — Overwriting a valid stored refresh token with a placeholder breaks later refreshes for callers like Zoom, which copy `newTokens.refresh_token` into the credential. Apply the `"refresh_token"` default only in sync mode, and otherwise keep the existing stored token.

App metadata looked up by slug but appStoreMetadata is keyed by directory name — For apps whose slug differs from the directory name, such as Google Calendar and Zoom, the lookup returns undefined and the webhook returns 404, so their credentials never sync. `appStoreMetadata` is keyed by directory name, so find the entry in `Object.values(appStoreMetadata)` whose `slug` matches `app.slug`.

Webhook header name lookup is case-sensitive against lowercased req.headers — Node lowercases names in `req.headers`, so a mixed-case `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` like `X-Webhook-Secret` never matches and every request gets a 403. Lowercase the configured name before indexing `req.headers`.

Credential key is overwritten with a SafeParse wrapper instead of parsed data — `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a SafeParse wrapper (`{success, data}`), so `key` holds the wrapper and `prisma.credential.update` stores it, corrupting the credential. Use the `.data` of the result as `key`.
credentialId passed to refreshOAuthTokens as userId argument — Pass `credential.userId` instead, threading it into `refreshAccessToken`.

Schema uses computed keys that become literal strings and reject valid token responses — `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` evaluate to literal strings like "ZodString", not wildcards, so the schema demands a property with that name and rejects real token responses when sharing is on. Use `access_token: z.string()` with `.passthrough()` and an explicit expiry check.

Sync-mode token refresh returns raw fetch Response instead of expected shape — Returning the raw fetch `Response` in sync mode breaks callers expecting other shapes: Google reads `res.data`, HubSpot reads `.accessToken` and `.expiresIn`, and Zoho CRM and Bigin read `tokenInfo.data`. Parse `response.json()` and return the shape each caller expects.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:86-94`

Salesforce token refreshed on every client creation and stale access token used — Every `getClient` call hits the Salesforce token endpoint, bypassing credential sync, and the `jsforce.Connection` receives the stale `credentialKey.access_token`. Refresh only when expired, route it through `refreshOAuthTokens`, and pass `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`.

Invalid token response now throws and loses error logging on refresh — A malformed Microsoft response now rejects the whole refresh and its details go unlogged, whereas before the zod error was logged and execution continued. Wrap `parseRefreshTokenResponse` in a try/catch, or use `safeParse`, and keep the error logging.

Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time !== operator — Comparing the webhook secret with `!==` leaks timing information on a network-exposed endpoint. Compare SHA-256 digests with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` and reject non-string header values.

goldensDetail.text: The webhook parses the body with zod .parse and decrypts/JSON-parses the keys without error handling, so invalid payloads produce 500 errors instead of 400 responses.
parseRefreshTokenResponse writes the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when the refresh response omits a refresh token, so the stored credential gets an invalid refresh token and later refreshes fail.

minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys from z.string().toString(), which produce a literal key rather than a wildcard, so the sync-mode schema does not validate or keep expiry and other token fields as intended.
Google Calendar persists the safeParse result object instead of its data as the credential key, corrupting the stored credential so later reads fail.
Salesforce getClient now refreshes the OAuth token and writes the credential on every service construction, adding a network round trip and DB write even when the access token is valid.
The new Salesforce token refresh uses prisma without importing it, so the code fails type checking and throws a ReferenceError at runtime.
Salesforce checks response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok when refreshing the token, which can misclassify successful responses, and then ignores the refreshed token.
After refreshing the Salesforce token, jsforce.Connection is created with the stale access_token and instance_url instead of the newly refreshed values.

The app-credential webhook looks up appStoreMetadata by app.slug, but the map is keyed by dirName, so apps whose slug differs from their directory (e.g. google-calendar) always get a 404 and their credentials cannot be synced.

findings.description: SMS cron deleteMany removes non-SMS reminders with retryCount > 1 — Without an SMS filter, this cleanup can silently delete email and WhatsApp reminders that have `retryCount` above 1. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to this branch of the `deleteMany` condition.

Failed retryCount update in catch block aborts the whole SMS batch — If the `prisma.workflowReminder.update` in the catch block throws, the error escapes, aborts the loop, and fails the whole cron request, so one bad reminder blocks the rest. Log first and wrap the `retryCount` update in its own try/catch.

goldensDetail.text: retryCount is set to reminder.retryCount + 1 from a value read at the start of the run instead of an atomic increment, so overlapping runs can lose increments.
The deleteMany OR clause applies retryCount > 1 without the SMS method filter, so the SMS cron deletes any workflow reminder (email, WhatsApp) with retryCount above 1.

The retry-count update inside the catch block is not guarded, so if it throws (for example the reminder was deleted concurrently) the error escapes the loop and the cron run fails, skipping the remaining reminders.
Claims transient errors increment retryCount, so two runs during an outage delete the whole pending SMS reminder queue.

SMS-sending locks are counted as failed scheduling attempts: scheduleSMS returns undefined for locked users/teams, retryCount is incremented, and after two cron runs the retryCount > 1 cleanup deletes future reminders even if sending is later unlocked.

findings.description: Backup code login bypasses password verification — One backup code is enough to log in because the password check is skipped whenever `credentials.totpCode` is non-empty, and the backup-code branch never validates `totpCode`. Verify the password whenever `credentials.backupCode` is present, e.g. `if (user.password && (!credentials.totpCode || credentials.backupCode))`.

Backup code consumption is non-atomic and allows reuse under concurrency — Because the read-modify-write on `backupCodes` isn't atomic, a single-use code can work twice, and parallel logins can overwrite each other's update and restore a consumed code. Make the update conditional on the previously read `backupCodes` value and fail the login if no row was updated.

2FA enable assertion checks a Promise and can never fail — `isChecked()` returns a Promise, which is always truthy, so the assertion passes even when 2FA isn't shown as enabled. Close the dialog via `backup-codes-close`, then assert `two-factor-switch` with `data-state="checked"` is visible.

Backup code download and copy checks do not verify file or clipboard content — The test passes even if the downloaded file or copied text is empty or wrong, since it only checks the static filename and a success toast. Read the downloaded file and the clipboard, and assert each holds 10 codes in XXXXX-XXXXX format.

Dismissing backup codes dialog skips onEnable and leaves stale state — Dismissing with Esc or an overlay click skips `onEnable()` and `resetState()`, so `viewer.me` isn't invalidated, the 2FA switch looks disabled, and reopening shows old codes from the stale `DisplayBackupCodes` step. Call `onEnable()` when the enable request succeeds, or run the same close logic from `onOpenChange`.

Backup code compared with non-constant-time indexOf — `indexOf` short-circuits, so response timing can leak information about the stored backup codes. Compare each stored code using `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers, without early exit, to find the matching index.

**Also found in:**
- `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:60-64`

goldensDetail.text: The credentials authorize() skips the password check when any totpCode is present, and the new backup-code branch never validates that totpCode, so a backup code plus a dummy totpCode logs in without the account password.

findings.description: getBaseConditions test seeds one booking, so it can't detect dropped conditions — With only one booking matching both conditions, the test still passes if `getBaseConditions` drops a condition or returns an always-true one. Seed a booking matching only the auth condition and another matching only the filter condition, then assert both are excluded from the results.

goldensDetail.text: The getBaseConditions test uses a single booking matching both auth and filter conditions, so it would pass even if the conditions were not combined.
The new public options type makes teamId optional for team scope, so a missing teamId compiles and silently yields empty insights instead of a type error.
Claims getBaseConditions returns OR fragments without parentheses, so a caller appending `AND <extra>` would leak rows outside the authorization scope.

findings.description: Raw HTML posts skip sanitization in Post#cook, enabling stored XSS — `Post#cook` returns `raw` unsanitized, so HTML from an external feed or fetched page is stored in `cooked` and rendered on the forum's origin, enabling stored XSS against users and staff. Sanitize the HTML with a whitelist-based tool in the raw_html branch of `cook` or in `TopicEmbed.import`.

Adding NOT NULL column with default rewrites large posts table under exclusive lock — On the Postgres versions this app targets, this rewrites the whole `posts` table under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, blocking all reads and writes during the deploy. Add `cook_method` as nullable, set the default, backfill in batches, then add the `NOT NULL` constraint.

Unescaped URL interpolated into anchor HTML allows HTML injection — A feed-supplied `url` containing `'` or `<` can break out of the `href` attribute and inject HTML or script into the post. Escape `url` with `ERB::Util.html_escape`, or build the anchor with `link_to`, before interpolating it.

Concurrent imports of same URL race and raise RecordNotUnique — The check-then-create on `embed_url` is not atomic, so concurrent imports from `PollFeed` and `RetrieveTopic` both create a topic and the loser hits the unique index with an unhandled `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`. Rescue `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` and return the existing embed's post, or lock on the URL.

NoMethodError on feed items without content aborts the polling loop — `i.content.scrub` raises `NoMethodError` for items lacking `content`, which aborts the `rss.items.each` loop and skips every later item. Fall back with `(i.content || i.description || '')` and skip items with a blank body or `url`.
absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/x.png — Skip values starting with `//` so only genuinely site-relative paths get the prefix.

Origin check uses substring match, allowing spoofed postMessage origins — The `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` check is a substring match, so any origin that is a prefix of `discourseUrl` passes and can spoof messages. Parse `discourseUrl` into its origin and require `e.origin` to equal it exactly.

feed_polling_url test doesn't enable polling so it can't fail on the URL check — This test never enables `feed_polling_enabled?`, which defaults to false, so `execute` skips `poll_feed` regardless of the URL and the test passes even without the `feed_polling_url.present?` check. Stub `feed_polling_enabled?` to true and set `embed_by_username` so only the missing URL blocks the call.

**Also found in:**
- `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:24-28`

goldensDetail.text: The referer and embed_url host checks compare against SiteSetting.embeddable_host case-sensitively, so a host differing only in case is rejected even though hostnames are case-insensitive.

PollFeed reads i.content.scrub for every feed item, so items without a content element (common in RSS feeds that only have description) raise NoMethodError and abort the import of the remaining items.

TopicEmbed.import appends a footer that interpolates the URL unescaped into an <a href='...'> tag in raw HTML that is later rendered unsanitized, so a crafted URL can inject markup; it also appends to contents with << without handling nil.
When the embedded post has been deleted, TopicEmbed.import's update path passes a nil embed.post to PostRevisor and crashes on every later import of that URL.
Claims import_remote crashes on unparseable pages (nil content) and dead URLs because it does no nil check or network error handling around open(url).read.

absolutize_urls only handles root-relative paths: protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/x.png are rewritten to http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png and path-relative links are left unresolved, breaking links and images in imported posts.

Every retrieval of an article not yet embedded synchronously polls and imports the entire RSS feed, and since throttling is per URL, many different article requests repeat the full feed download and processing.

The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' specs leave feed_polling_enabled at its false default, so they never reach the condition they name and would pass with those checks deleted.
`import_remote` fetches the embed URL with open-uri, which follows redirects, so the embeddable-host check on the initial URL can be bypassed to reach internal services (SSRF).
The retrieve throttle is keyed by the full embed URL, so an anonymous client can vary the query string on the embeddable host to bypass it and make the server create an unbounded number of topics.

The "requires feed_polling_enabled?" spec leaves feed_polling_url and embed_by_username at their blank defaults, so poll_feed is skipped regardless and the test would pass even without the enabled check.
The embed layout references the 'embed' stylesheet and embed.js, but neither is in config.assets.precompile, so with precompiled assets in production the embed page fails to load them.

findings.description: Migration inserts embeddable hosts with scheme and path, breaking host matching — Migrated hosts that keep a scheme or path, like `https://example.com/1234`, never match `URI(...).host` in `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`, so embedding breaks after upgrade. Strip the scheme, path and whitespace from each `h` and quote the value with `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote`.

Migration crashes when embed_category or uncategorized setting has no rows — When `embed_category` is unset or names no category, the query returns no rows and indexing `[0]` raises NoMethodError, so the migration fails. Check `cmd_tuples` on the result before reading it, for both the `embed_category` and `uncategorized_category_id` lookups.

record_for_host ignores host case and port when matching stored hosts — A referer like `http://EvilTrout.com/` won't match a stored lowercase host, and a stored `host:port` entry can never match, so embedding fails for valid hosts. Downcase `uri.host` and also match `"#{uri.host}:#{uri.port}"` in `record_for_host`.

before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil — A missing or nil `host` makes `self.host.sub!` raise NoMethodError, so the request returns a 500 instead of a validation error. Skip the cleanup when `host` is nil, or assign `host.to_s.sub(...)` instead of mutating in place.

update and destroy raise NoMethodError (500) when the host id is missing — A missing or already-deleted id leaves `host` nil, so `save_host` and `host.destroy` raise NoMethodError and return a 500. Use `find_by` in `update` and `destroy`, and raise `Discourse::NotFound` when the record is nil.

goldensDetail.text: The migration reads execute(...)[0]['id'] for embed_category without checking for an empty result, so installs without that setting stored crash the migration instead of falling back to the uncategorized category.

After saving a host, the component overwrites its category with findById(categoryId); when no category was chosen this is null even though the server saved the uncategorized category, so the row shows no category until reload.
Hosts saved with a port (allowed by the validation regex) are stored as host:port, but lookup compares only URI.host, so those configured hosts never match and embedding fails for them.
EmbeddableHost's host format validation only accepts TLDs of 2-5 letters, so admins cannot add embeddable hosts on longer TLDs like example.technology.

The flex-item styles target the inner .extra-info-wrapper instead of the component's root div, so in the flexbox header a long topic title keeps its full width and pushes the navigation panel out instead of being truncated.
The align-items mixin emits no -moz-box-align, so on old Firefox versions using the display:-moz-box fallback the advertised vertical centering is not applied.

Removing the float-based right alignment of .d-header .panel leaves the server-rendered (no-JS) header's login panel, which sits inside .row and is not a flex item, no longer right-aligned next to the title.

Making .small-action a flex container leaves .small-action-desc content-sized (no flex:1), so the right-floated edit/delete buttons inside it sit right after short action descriptions instead of at the right edge of the row.

On mobile the .small-action custom message keeps margin-left:-40px, tuned for the old 4em left padding; with the new flex layout and 1.5% padding it is pulled into the avatar column and overlaps the icon.

findings.description: Duplicate downsize definition overrides first and breaks 5-argument callers — The second `downsize` definition replaces the first, so the existing 5-argument caller in `resize_emoji.rb` raises `ArgumentError`.
