Keep a single `downsize` that accepts both forms, or update that caller to pass "100x100".

Percentage resize with allow_animation fails for GIFs so downsizing loop never shrinks — gifsicle rejects a percentage resize, so `downsize` returns false and `tempfile` never shrinks across all 5 attempts, leaving oversized animated GIFs untouched. Pass `allow_animation: false` here and break out of the loop when `downsize` returns false.

Client-side upload size check ignores max_attachment_size_kb setting — The hardcoded 10MB limit skips the per-type `max_attachment_size_kb` setting, so oversized attachments pass the client check and only fail after upload. Use the site setting for non-image types and apply the 10MB cap only when `type` is an image.

goldensDetail.text: downsize is defined twice in OptimizedImage; the new (from, to, dimensions, opts) version overrides the (max_width, max_height) one, so existing callers such as ResizeEmoji that pass width and height now raise ArgumentError.

The client-side upload size check hardcodes 10 MB instead of the per-type max_<type>_size_kb setting, so attachment limits diverge from the server: larger allowed attachments are blocked and smaller limits are only enforced server-side.
The upload downsizing passes a percentage ('80%') as dimensions, but for animated GIFs the gifsicle path uses --resize-fit, which expects WxH geometry, so downsizing silently fails.
Auto-downsizing passes the upload tempfile path, which lacks a .gif extension, so the animated branch is never chosen and convert keeps only the first frame, flattening oversized animated GIFs.
Claims the downsize loop checking tempfile.size may never terminate because of a stale cached size, causing infinite loops.
Oversized SVG uploads go through the new ImageMagick downsize loop because SVG counts as an image, so the vector file is rasterized or corrupted in place before Upload.create_for parses it as SVG.

The upload tempfile path, which for API URL uploads embeds the request-controlled type param, is now passed to OptimizedImage.downsize and run unescaped in a shell via backticks, allowing command injection through type.
The 413 upload error message states a hard-coded 10 MB maximum that may not match the limit the server or web server actually enforces.

findings.description: Default `limit` of 50 truncates large groups on the public members page — Groups with more than 50 members now show only the first 50 on the public page, since it has no pagination UI. Previously non-automatic groups returned everyone and automatic groups up to 200.

Unbounded and negative limit/offset params in group members endpoint — Any caller who can see a group can request a huge `limit` and force loading and serializing every member, risking memory and CPU exhaustion, while a negative `limit` or `offset` reaches SQL and causes a 500. Clamp `limit` to a maximum such as 200 and keep `offset` at 0 or above.

`findMembers` builds its URL from the editable `name`, breaking reloads after edits — If an admin edits the name before saving and then pages or adds or removes a member, the reload requests `/groups/<unsaved name>/members.json`, which returns a 404 or the wrong group. Request members by group `id`, or keep the persisted name separate from the editable one.

Remove-member spec uses `xhr :put` instead of `xhr :delete` for `remove_member` — Controller specs ignore the HTTP verb, so this test would still pass even if the route or verb were wrong. The real `remove_member` route is `DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members`, so use `xhr :delete` here.

`totalPages` over-counts by one when `user_count` is a multiple of `limit` — Admins see a phantom empty last page, `showingLast` stays false on the real last page, and `next` fetches an empty page. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` in `totalPages`, and compute `currentPage` consistently with it.

goldensDetail.text: The admin group pager computes total pages as floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so when the member count is an exact multiple of the limit it shows an extra page and Next navigates to an empty member list.
Paging actions fire overlapping member requests and each response unconditionally overwrites offset and members, so a stale response arriving last can revert the list to an earlier page.
The public members endpoint now always caps results at 50 per page, but the public group members page has no pagination, so groups with more than 50 members are silently truncated for users.
Creating a group ignores the alias_level the admin selected, saving only name and visibility, so new groups keep the default alias level.
Removing a member deletes the membership row directly and skips clearing the user's primary_group_id, so a removed user can keep this group as their primary group.
Group member pagination is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit: Next moves to offset == user_count and shows an empty page.
Admin remove_member deletes memberships with group.users.delete, which skips GroupUser callbacks, so the cached groups.user_count is never decremented and stays inflated.

Admin add_members pushes every username into group.users without skipping existing members, so adding someone already in the group hits the unique group_users index, returns a 500 and leaves earlier users partially added.
The public group members endpoint takes `limit` from params with no upper bound or positivity check, letting a visitor request huge pages or trigger a 500 with a negative limit.
Admin remove_member calls group.users.delete with a raw integer id, which raises RecordNotFound (404/500) when the user is not or no longer a member, e.g. on concurrent removal.

findings.description:
Fallback locales not loaded outside controllers, caching missing translations — Outside controllers (jobs, mailers), `I18n.translate` can fall back to an unloaded locale, and the 'translation missing' string is cached under the real key for every later reader. Make `translate` call `ensure_loaded!` for each locale in the fallback chain before lookup, or skip caching missing-translation results.

**Also found in:**
- `app/controllers/application_controller.rb:159-159`

goldensDetail.text: Fallback locale catalogs are only loaded in the controller's set_locale filter, while translate loads just the current locale, so translations outside requests (jobs, mailers) cannot fall back to the site default or English.

The translation cache key does not include the site or its default locale, but fallback results now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, so multisite processes or a changed default locale serve stale fallback translations.

findings.description: Device limit check and insert are not atomic, allowing limit to be exceeded — Concurrent requests from new devices can all pass the `CountDevices` check before any insert lands, so the number of devices can exceed `deviceLimit`. Make the count check and the insert atomic with a single conditional insert, a transaction, or a lock.

Rejected device stays in local cache after device limit error — `tagDeviceUI` sets the local cache key before `CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs, so a device rejected with `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is cached. For 29 minutes `TagDevice` then returns nil and it authenticates despite the limit.

Anonymous device tagging now blocks requests and can reject authentication — Every anonymous request that misses the local cache now blocks on the database count and write, and `Authenticate` can fail with `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. Restore the detached, non-blocking tagging unless rejecting at the limit is intended.

goldensDetail.text: tagDeviceUI caches the device key before CreateOrUpdateDevice; when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the entry stays, so the next request from the same device skips the limit check and authenticates for up to 29 minutes.
The new auth.anonymous device_limit setting has no entry in conf/defaults.ini, so the GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT environment override is ignored and the limit stays 0.

findings.description: Async legacy create goroutine uses request context that gets cancelled — The goroutines derive their context from the request `ctx`, so once the request ends the legacy `Create`, `Update`, `Delete` and `DeleteCollection` calls get a cancelled context and the writes silently fail. Wrap `ctx` in `context.WithoutCancel` before applying the timeout.

Legacy update in mode 3 ignores the object produced by unified storage — `Legacy.Update` recomputes the update from the original `objInfo` against its own old object, so it can store different data than unified storage and the stores diverge. Pass an `updateWrapper` carrying the object returned by `Storage.Update`.

Legacy create goroutine shares obj pointer with the response, causing a data race — `Legacy.Create` may mutate `obj` while the handler serializes `created`, which can be the same object, so this is a data race that can corrupt the response. Pass `obj.DeepCopyObject()` to the goroutine.

Mode3 Create test never asserts the async Legacy Create call happened — The legacy write runs in a goroutine the test never waits for, so removing it from `Create` would not fail the test. Wait with `assert.Eventually` and call `m.AssertCalled` for the Legacy `Create`.

Mode3 Update test never verifies the asynchronous Legacy Update call — The legacy update runs asynchronously and is never awaited or asserted, so dropping it would not fail the test. Wait for the goroutine and assert the Legacy `Update` call happened; the Delete and DeleteCollection tests have the same gap.

Create records storage failure with legacy duration metric — A `Storage.Create` failure is reported as a legacy error, leaving the storage error metric empty. Call `d.recordStorageDuration(true, ...)` instead of `recordLegacyDuration`; `Update` has the same mistake.

**Also found in:**
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:129-129`
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:126-131`

Legacy DeleteCollection duration recorded in storage metrics instead of legacy — Legacy latency and errors get mixed into the storage metrics, and the legacy metrics miss delete-collection entirely. Use `recordLegacyDuration` instead of `recordStorageDuration` in this goroutine.

Delete success metric uses object name instead of kind as label — Passing `name` creates a high-cardinality metric label that doesn't match the other series, which all use `options.Kind`. Pass `options.Kind` to `recordStorageDuration`.

goldensDetail.text: The legacy DeleteCollection goroutine records its duration with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, misattributing legacy latency and errors to the storage metric.
Delete's success path records the storage metric with the object name in the kind label instead of options.Kind, creating per-object series and inconsistent labels.
On storage Create/Update failure the duration is recorded with recordLegacyDuration, attributing unified-store errors to the legacy metric.

Mode 3 legacy writes now run in background goroutines derived from the request context, which is cancelled when the request completes, so legacy writes can be cancelled and legacy storage falls out of sync.
Legacy.Update now receives the original objInfo instead of a wrapper carrying the object stored in unified storage, so legacy recomputes the update and can diverge.
The Mode 3 tests never wait for or assert the asynchronous legacy writes, and legacy and storage share one mock, so removing the legacy calls would not fail them.
Independent per-request goroutines remove ordering between legacy writes to the same resource, so legacy can end up with an older version or a resurrected object.
Mode 3 legacy-storage write errors (create/update/delete/delete-collection) are no longer logged after moving to async goroutines; only a duration metric with an error flag is recorded.
DualWriterMode3.Delete now returns on any unified-storage error, including NotFound, before deleting from legacy, so objects that exist only in legacy can no longer be deleted.

findings.description: TotalDocs reads index cache map without lock while event goroutine writes it — A watch event during startup can make `BuildIndex` write the `bleveBackend.cache` map while `TotalDocs` iterates it, causing a fatal concurrent map access that crashes the process. Take `b.cacheMu.RLock()` inside `TotalDocs`, or compute the count before starting the `handleEvent` goroutine.

Parallel init workers race on shared err and batch counter in search.go — With the lock gone from `BuildIndex`, the `errgroup` workers in `searchSupport.init` race on the shared `err` and `totalBatchesIndexed`, so one worker can overwrite another's error with nil and hide a failed build. Use a goroutine-local `err` from `s.build(...)` and an atomic or mutex-guarded counter.

Concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key are no longer serialised — Concurrent builds for one `NamespacedResource` can now collide: file-backed builds fail or corrupt each other in `bleve.New`, and in-memory builds silently overwrite the cached index. Serialize builds per key, or re-check `b.cache` under `cacheMu` before building, and publish the index only once.

Unconditional postgres skip removes coverage of resource server startup path — Skipping postgres unconditionally leaves the changed startup path (`NewResourceServer` now calling `Init`, search init before the watcher) untested there, so postgres failures would go unnoticed. Find the Drone failure cause, such as the fixed 500ms sleep or DB host config; if a skip is unavoidable, limit it to Drone.

goldensDetail.text: BuildIndex now locks only the final cache assignment, so concurrent callers for the same uncached key all build the same expensive index in parallel and the last one overwrites the others.

The new startup log calls TotalDocs, which iterates the index cache without a lock, after the event goroutine that can add indexes has started, so a concurrent map read and write can crash the process.
The PR skips the storage-server module integration test on postgres instead of fixing the failure, removing coverage of the new eager initialization on postgres.

findings.description: Grafana recording rules lose Export, Pause and Restore abilities — Grafana recording rules are Grafana-managed but not alerting rules, so `isAlertingRule` strips their Export and Pause abilities in the list view, unlike the ruler-based hook. Use `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` for `ModifyExport`, `Pause` and `Restore`, and keep `isAlertingRule` only for `Silence`.

Duplicate ability enabled when rule is undefined (skipToken) for Grafana prom rules — With an undefined `rule` (the `skipToken` case), `Duplicate` stays enabled, and `AlertRuleMenu` ORs it with the ruler ability, so cloud and Mimir rules get a Duplicate item even when unsupported. Set `MaybeSupported` to `NotSupported` when `rule` is undefined.

**Also found in:**
- `public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rule-viewer/AlertRuleMenu.tsx:89-92`

goldensDetail.text: The pause menu item is still gated on a Grafana ruler rule, but the list view now passes only the Prometheus rule, so Pause/Resume disappears for list-view rules even when the user may pause them.
The Delete menu item still requires a ruler rule, which list-view Grafana rules no longer provide, so users with delete permission lose the Delete action.

When the Grafana prom-rule branch is skipped (datasource rules), useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) still reports Duplicate as supported and allowed by Grafana create permission, and AlertRuleMenu ORs it with the ruler ability, so Duplicate appears on cloud rules even when the ruler check denies it.

For list-view Grafana rules RuleActionsButtons gets only promRule, so the Silence menu item is shown but the silence drawer, still gated on a ruler alerting rule, never renders and clicking Silence does nothing.

findings.description: Null rawTokenId check mistakenly validates grantType again — A null `rawTokenId` passes validation unnoticed, because the check tests `grantType` a second time and the message names a field it never checks. Pass `rawTokenId` to `Objects.requireNonNull` instead.

Grant shortcut check in isAccessTokenId is inverted and uses wrong indices — The matcher in `isAccessTokenId` never verifies the grant type, because `substring(3, 5)` straddles two fields and the comparison is inverted. Use `substring(4, 6)` after checking the length, and return false when it does not equal `expectedGrantShortcut`.

Null model NPE remains in getSubGroupsStream overloads after concurrent delete — A group deleted by another thread still triggers the same NPE through the three `getSubGroupsStream` overloads, because they call `modelSupplier.get()` without a null check. Apply the same null handling there, for example by returning `Stream.empty()` when the model is null.

Group read/delete race test lacks synchronization and thread join — The test can pass with no overlap, or miss a late exception, even if the `getSubGroupsCount` null-model fix is reverted. Have the reader count down a `CountDownLatch` after its first successful read, delete only after that, and join the thread before asserting on `caughtExceptions`.

Reader thread is not joined before asserting on caught exceptions — An exception from the last in-flight read can arrive after the assertion on `caughtExceptions`, and the thread can outlive the test. Keep the `Thread` reference and call `join()` after `deletedAll.set(true)` before asserting.

Prefix/suffix trimming can overlap and cause StringIndexOutOfBoundsException — When the sanitizer removes one character from a run of repeats, such as `value="aa"` and `sanitized="a"`, the prefix and suffix loops overlap and `substring` throws `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException`. The verifier then crashes instead of reporting the key.

Lithuanian totpStep1 message replaced with Italian text — Lithuanian users will see Italian text on the OTP setup page because `totpStep1` holds an Italian sentence. Replace it with a Lithuanian translation, such as the one in the fix.

loginTotpStep1 in Lithuanian bundle contains Italian text — Lithuanian users will see Italian text on the login-time TOTP setup screen because `loginTotpStep1` holds an Italian sentence. Replace it with a Lithuanian translation.

Admin UI message uses MessageFormat syntax instead of i18next placeholders — If the admin UI renders `error-invalid-multivalued-size` with i18next, the `{0}` placeholders won't be interpolated and the `{2,choice,...}` clause will print literally. Keep i18next-style `{{0}}` placeholders here, or confirm the consumer formats this key with MessageFormat.

**Also found in:**
- `js/apps/account-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v3/account/messages/messages_en.properties:188-188`

goldensDetail.text: The diff-trimming code computes common prefix and suffix independently, so they can overlap and substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the verifier instead of reporting the illegal HTML.

The account and admin UI bundles now use Java MessageFormat placeholders and choice syntax for error-invalid-multivalued-size, but i18next expects {{n}}, so the UI shows literal {0}/{1}/{2} and the raw choice text.

findings.description: Client removal handler throws when V2 fine-grained authz is enabled — With both feature flags on, `management()` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2`, and `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled` always throws `UnsupportedOperationException`, so client deletion fails. Skip this V1 cleanup in the `ClientRemovedEvent` handler when V2 is enabled, or make `setPermissionsEnabled` a no-op.

NPE when Clients type resource is missing in hasPermission — `getResourceTypeResource` can return null, and passing it to `findByResource` causes an NPE and a 500 instead of a denial. Return false when the resource is null before calling `findByResource`.

getClientsWithPermission matches no per-client resources — Per-client resources from `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` have no type, so `findByType` misses them and only finds the type-level "Clients" resource, which is not a client id. Callers like `AvailableRoleMappingResource` get wrong results; iterate clients and look up each resource by owner and name.

canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException in V2 instead of denying — `AbstractTokenExchangeProvider` still calls `canExchangeTo`, so under V2 token exchange fails with `UnsupportedOperationException` instead of a permission denial. Return false in `canExchangeTo`, or guard the caller.

goldensDetail.text: Claims the removal-cleanup listener is guarded by the V1 fine-grained flag, so client/role/group permissions are orphaned when V1 is disabled or only V2 is enabled.

getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 only finds the type-level 'Clients' resource and returns its name, never actual client ids, so callers that resolve the returned values as client ids get wrong results or null clients.
Claims getResourceTypeResource can return null in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, causing a NullPointerException in findByResource.
ClientPermissionsV2.canView() ignores a global MANAGE permission, so admins with only global manage take the unpaginated, per-client evaluated listing path.
canView(client) short-circuits on the global all-clients VIEW permission, so a client-specific permission denying an admin is never evaluated and the client is still viewable.

The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, an admin granted a permission on all clients is denied on any client that also has its own per-client permission resource, because only the per-client resource is evaluated.

ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AbstractTokenExchangeProvider still calls clients().canExchangeTo for client-to-client exchange, so with token exchange and FGAP V2 enabled the request fails with a server error instead of a permission decision.

findings.description: PasswordForm no longer skipped for passkey-only users on themes lacking passkey UI — Passkey-only users now reach a password page that offers no passkey option under themes inheriting the base `login-password.ftl`, so they cannot finish the step. Add the passkeys macro to that template, or apply the `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` condition in `configuredFor` only when the theme can render it.

Passkey credential IDs exposed on password form before user is authenticated — Anyone who knows a username can read that user's passkey credential IDs and learn whether the user has passkeys, because `fillContextForm` runs before the password is verified. Call it only when `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` is set, and otherwise use discoverable-credential mode without an `allowCredentials` list.

goldensDetail.text: The test registers cleanup for the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases, so the created identity providers are never cleaned up.

Adding the organization/BROKER_PUBLIC check to the shared LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate also changes IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate, so with organizations disabled a user's linked IdP that has an organizationId but is not public is no longer shown on the login page.

findings.description: Error timestamps (seconds) compared against rrweb timestamps (milliseconds) — If the units differ, error entries sort before every breadcrumb and the AI summary gets the wrong chronology. Normalize both sides in `gen_request_data`, for example by multiplying the `error_events` timestamp by 1000 before comparing it to the rrweb `timestamp`.

Age/timestamp exclusivity check ignores a value of 0 — A valid value of 0 is falsy, so a report with both fields passes when one of them is 0. In `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age`, check `is not None` on `self.initial_data.get(...)` instead of truthiness.

Test with max_segment_id=None never exercises the null guard — Because `delete_matched_rows` is patched, the `max_segment_id` None row never reaches `_make_recording_filenames`, so the test passes even without the guard. Add a test that runs `_make_recording_filenames` or an unmocked `delete_matched_rows` with None and asserts no filenames are produced.

Error details paired with wrong event IDs via zip over dict values — `nodestore.backend.get_multi` doesn't guarantee that the order of `events.values()` matches `error_ids`, and missing nodes may be omitted. This can attach the wrong title, message and timestamp to an event ID.

goldensDetail.text: The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators check truthiness via initial_data.get(), so a zero value is treated as absent and a report carrying both fields passes validation.
The validation-failure warning logs the entire raw, attacker-controlled browser report instead of a redacted subset.
The Snuba replay lookup for error IDs runs even when enable_error_context=false, adding a needless query (and failure point) to opt-out requests.

With the use-table-widget-visualization flag on, the widget renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded empty columns and data instead of the query results, so every table widget shows an empty table.
The custom cell renderers fall back to default rendering on any falsy return (0, '', null), not only undefined, so a renderer cannot render zero or an empty cell.
The attribute-keys query key no longer includes the organization slug, so two organizations with the same filters share a cache entry and switching orgs can show the previous org's attribute names.

Every paginated breadcrumb-summary request queries the replay and fetches all of its error events from nodestore with no cap, adding latency and memory proportional to the replay's error count on each page.
HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES is applied only when a search query is present; the no-search early return shows all attributes, so the hidden attributes still appear in the default span attributes view.

The bulk delete test sets max_segment_id to None to cover the new guard in _make_recording_filenames, but it mocks delete_matched_rows, so the guard is never executed and removing it would not fail the test.
Error event timestamps (seconds) are compared with replay recording event timestamps (milliseconds), so errors are not interleaved chronologically with breadcrumbs.

findings.description: Hung flusher process is never killed because isinstance check excludes SpawnProcess — `SpawnProcess` subclasses `BaseProcess`, not `multiprocessing.Process`, so the `isinstance` guard is likely False and a hung flusher is never killed. The old process keeps its shards while `_create_process_for_shards` starts a replacement, which can produce duplicate segments.
time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched in the test — Replace it with a deadline-based poll until `messages` is non-empty, or capture the real sleep before patching.

`break` on an expired join deadline skips `process.terminate()` for remaining flushers — Flusher processes keep running after `join()` returns, whereas the old code always terminated them after the wait loop. Remove the `break` and always call `process.terminate()` after each wait, or add a separate terminate loop after the wait loop.

goldensDetail.text: The restart path only kills a hung flusher if it is a multiprocessing.Process, but spawn-context workers are SpawnProcess, so hung processes are never killed and a duplicate flusher is started for the same shards.
join() breaks out of the per-process loop when the shared deadline expires, skipping termination of the remaining flusher processes and leaving them running after shutdown.

findings.description: Dataclass default timezone.now() is evaluated once at import time — Every `AssignmentSource` gets the same stale process-start timestamp in `queued`, and that value goes out in the task payload. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each instance gets its own time.

Installer check skipped when no Integration row exists for installation_id — Return `error(...)` here instead, or verify the OAuth user against the installation's account or sender from the GitHub API.

Token request and `get_user_info` can raise unhandled errors, causing a 500 — A network failure or non-2xx response from the GitHub token or `/user` endpoints leaves `safe_urlopen` and `get_user_info` (which calls `raise_for_status()`) unhandled, giving a 500 instead of the error page. Wrap both calls in try/except and return `error(request, self.active_organization)`.

OAuth state is a predictable static signature, not a per-flow nonce — `pipeline.signature` is identical for every user and session, so the OAuth `state` is predictable and gives no CSRF or session binding. An attacker could then bind their own GitHub login to a victim's flow.

test_installation_not_found uses wrong state and asserts generic error text — The state in `test_installation_not_found` likely differs from the pipeline signature, so the test probably fails at the state check, and the generic "Invalid installation request." text matches every `OAuthLoginView` error. Use the real pipeline signature as `state` and assert on something specific to a missing installation.

KeyError when Integration metadata lacks sender during installation check — `build_integration` stores `sender` only when `state.get('sender')` is truthy, so an existing `Integration` without it makes `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` raise `KeyError` and return a 500. Read it with `.get('sender', {}).get('login')` and treat a missing value as a verification failure.

goldensDetail.text: test_installation_not_found uses a wrong OAuth state, so it fails at the state check and never reaches the installation-not-found path it is meant to test.

findings.description: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract and will fail to instantiate — `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` subclasses the abstract `StatefulDetectorHandler` but only has `pass`, so `group_type.detector_handler(self)` in `Detector.detector_handler` raises `TypeError` for every metric alert detector. Implement `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` and `build_occurrence_and_event_data`, or restore the no-op evaluate returning `{}`.

Expected occurrence uses value 6 but test evaluates 100; mock ignores value — The mock `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` ignores `value` (`evidence_data={}`), so the assertion passes whatever the handler sends to `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Put `value` in the mock occurrence's evidence data and build the expected occurrence with the real evaluated value, so a wrong value fails the test.

goldensDetail.text: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing its abstract methods, so instantiating it for metric alert detectors raises TypeError where it previously returned an empty-result handler.

The mock occurrence builder ignores its value argument, so tests (e.g. group_2 expected with 6 while the packet carries 10) pass regardless of which value is passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data.

findings.description: Monitor context returns raw config instead of transformed schedule_type copy — The transformed `config` copy is never used, so the occurrence's monitor context carries the raw numeric `schedule_type`. Return `config` instead of `monitor_environment.monitor.config` in `get_monitor_environment_context`.

Recurring collective cancellations miss other hosts' calendar events — Other hosts' events remain because `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` and the first `bookingRef` bypass the resolved host credential. Use `calendarCredential` and iterate each occurrence's references matching its credential ID.

Missing organizer calendar discards collective hosts' destination calendars — Other collective hosts receive no calendar events when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null because the optional `push` discards their destinations. Initialize `evt.destinationCalendar` to an empty array before appending `teamDestinationCalendars`.

Organization slug is not saved when team billing is disabled — Organizations created with team billing disabled lose their configured subdomain because `slug` is not persisted. Restore the `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` condition when writing `slug`.

Missing destination calendar crashes Google Meet booking creation — A null or empty destination array from `handleNewBooking.ts` leaves `mainHostDestinationCalendar` undefined, so Google Meet bookings throw instead of falling back to Cal Video. Restore optional access with `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

Secondary hosts receive the organizer's destination calendar — Pass `createEvent` a per-host event whose `destinationCalendar` contains only the current `destination`.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73-76`
- `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:72-76`

Missing calendar IDs lose destination fallback in updateEvent and deleteEvent — Legacy references without `externalCalendarId` lose their non-primary calendar target because `selectedCalendar` searches for that absent ID, potentially leaving events unchanged or undeleted. Restore a usable `event.destinationCalendar` fallback in both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent`.

Video booking references lose credential IDs needed for cancellation — Canceled bookings leave external video meetings behind because `deleteMeeting` requires a credential ID on the reference. Preserve `result.credentialId` for video results as well as calendar results.

User lookup exposes internal Prisma error messages to booking clients — Forwarding `Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError.message` can expose query details and database schema information to booking clients. Return a generic server error for Prisma failures, keep diagnostics in protected server logs, and preserve explicit `HttpError` messages separately.

goldensDetail.text: When externalCalendarId is absent, updateEvent/deleteEvent look for a destination calendar whose externalId equals that absent value, so the lookup never matches and the configured destination calendar is no longer used.
The organization slug is now set only when team billing is enabled (inverted condition), so with billing both slug and requestedSlug are set and without billing neither is.

Office365 (and Lark) createEvent ignore the new credentialId argument and always use the first destination calendar, so in collective bookings other hosts' credentials target the organizer's calendar instead of their own.

The Google Meet fallback reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining, so a Meet booking with a null or empty destinationCalendar throws instead of falling back to Cal Video.

For collective events whose organizer has no destination calendar, destinationCalendar is null and the optional push drops all other hosts' destination calendars, so those hosts never get calendar events.
Video booking references are now saved without their credentialId, so cancelling the booking can no longer find the video credential and the meeting is not deleted.

Cancelling all remaining occurrences of a recurring collective booking deletes only the first calendar reference of each booking, repeated once per host, so the other hosts' events stay on their calendars.

In Google createEvent, when no destination calendar matches the credentialId, the hangout-link events.patch is called with an undefined calendarId and fails, so the Meet link is not added to the event description.

When cancelling a recurring booking with multiple calendar references, the recurring-event deletion over all remaining bookings and credentials runs once per reference, causing duplicate delete calls and errors.

findings.description: Team admins are incorrectly forbidden from adding booking guests — Team admins who are neither the organizer nor an attendee receive `FORBIDDEN` because `isTeamOwner` rejects the `ADMIN` role. Use `isTeamAdmin` alone, since it accepts both `ADMIN` and `OWNER`.

Case-sensitive guest comparison allows blacklist bypass — An authorized attendee can bypass `blacklistedGuestEmails` by changing an address's letter case because `guest` is compared unchanged against the lowercased blacklist. Normalize submitted addresses before comparison and persistence.

Guest additions use attendee credentials to update the organizer's calendar — When a calendar reference lacks `credentialId`, `EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents` falls back to the attendee's credentials, potentially skipping the update or targeting the wrong account. Initialize `EventManager` with `booking.user` and the organizer's credentials from `getUsersCredentials`, rejecting bookings without an organizer.

Unbounded guest additions cause growing storage and email fan-out — Unbounded `guests` arrays grow storage and trigger concurrent emails through `sendAddGuestsEmails`, with later additions notifying the entire accumulated attendee list again. Enforce server-side per-request and per-booking guest limits before insertion, and bound notification concurrency.

Guest filtering allows duplicate attendees within and across requests — Repeated addresses and concurrent requests can produce duplicate attendees and invitations because `uniqueGuests` checks only the existing attendee snapshot. Deduplicate submitted addresses server-side and enforce booking/email uniqueness through a database constraint or serialized transaction.

Existing attendees receive fresh booking invitations when guests are added — Passing existing attendees in `guests` makes `sendAddGuestsEmails` send them `AttendeeScheduledEmail` rather than `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`, even though they were excluded from creation. Pass `uniqueGuests` so only newly added attendees receive fresh invitations.

goldensDetail.text: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, so only team owners pass; team admins who are not organizer or attendee are wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN.

The guest blacklist is lowercased but incoming guest emails are compared without normalization, so a blacklisted address submitted with different casing bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and is added and emailed.
The server never deduplicates the guests array, so a request with the same email twice inserts duplicate attendee rows for the booking.

The handler passes the unfiltered guests list to sendAddGuestsEmails, which uses it to pick who gets AttendeeScheduledEmail, so existing attendees included in the request receive a new-booking confirmation instead of the add-guests email.

EventManager is created with the requesting user's credentials, so when a non-organizer adds guests the organizer's calendar event is not updated (or the wrong account is used) for references without a credentialId.
sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings, so hosts and attendees receive add-guests emails even when standard emails are disabled.

The add-guests handler omits booking.iCalUID from the CalendarEvent, so the add-guests emails' .ics attachments use booking.uid as UID and recipients' calendars treat them as a new event rather than an update of the original booking invite.
Guest email uniqueness is checked case-sensitively, so case variants of the same address are accepted as distinct guests (and slip past the lowercased blacklist).

findings.description: Undefined prisma reference breaks Salesforce initialization — Salesforce initialization fails because `prisma` is neither imported nor declared in this file. Import the Prisma client before calling `prisma.credential.update`.

Missing refresh tokens are replaced with an invalid placeholder — Office365 merges `parseRefreshTokenResponse` output over existing credentials, so the literal `refresh_token` replaces a valid token and breaks later direct refreshes. Leave an omitted `refresh_token` absent and preserve the existing token at the caller.

Credential syncing returns a raw Response instead of expected token data — With syncing enabled, returning a raw `Response` breaks Google's `res.data.access_token` and Zoho's `.data.error` reads and supplies invalid fields where HubSpot expects `HubspotToken`. Normalize the sync response to the callers' expected representations, or update all callers consistently.

Computed Zod schema keys discard token expiry and refresh fields — Office365 and Zoom lose expiry data because `z.object` strips real response fields while these computed schema keys become literal strings. Explicitly model `expires_in`, `expiry_date`, and `refresh_token`, or preserve and validate additional properties.

Token refresh persists the validation wrapper instead of credentials — Subsequent credential validation fails because `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a validation wrapper, which `key` stores instead of the credential object. Check `success`, throw `error` on failure, and persist `data` on success.

OAuth refresh passes the credential ID instead of the owner's user ID — When syncing is enabled, passing `credentialId` as `calcomUserId` can fail refresh or select another user's credentials if IDs overlap; check `refreshOAuthTokens`' third parameter. Pass the credential owner's `userId`, preserving `null` for team-owned credentials.
Concurrent webhook deliveries can create duplicate credentials — Serialize creation for each user/app pair, or enforce uniqueness and use an atomic upsert.

Salesforce client initialization always refreshes tokens and writes credentials — Every Salesforce client initialization adds provider latency and a database write, even when `credentialKey` contains a usable access token. Move the token-refresh `fetch` and credential update to the expired-token or authentication-failure path.

Webhook secret comparison exposes secret-dependent timing — Comparing `req.headers` directly with `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` can expose secret-dependent timing on this public endpoint. Require a single-string header and compare buffers with `crypto.timingSafeEqual`, handling missing values and unequal lengths.

goldensDetail.text: The webhook parses the body with zod .parse and decrypts/JSON-parses the keys without error handling, so invalid payloads produce 500 errors instead of 400 responses.
parseRefreshTokenResponse writes the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when the refresh response omits a refresh token, so the stored credential gets an invalid refresh token and later refreshes fail.

minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys from z.string().toString(), which produce a literal key rather than a wildcard, so the sync-mode schema does not validate or keep expiry and other token fields as intended.
Google Calendar persists the safeParse result object instead of its data as the credential key, corrupting the stored credential so later reads fail.
Salesforce getClient now refreshes the OAuth token and writes the credential on every service construction, adding a network round trip and DB write even when the access token is valid.
The new Salesforce token refresh uses prisma without importing it, so the code fails type checking and throws a ReferenceError at runtime.
Salesforce checks response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok when refreshing the token, which can misclassify successful responses, and then ignores the refreshed token.
After refreshing the Salesforce token, jsforce.Connection is created with the stale access_token and instance_url instead of the newly refreshed values.

The app-credential webhook looks up appStoreMetadata by app.slug, but the map is keyed by dirName, so apps whose slug differs from their directory (e.g. google-calendar) always get a 404 and their credentials cannot be synced.

findings.description: SMS retry cleanup deletes reminders for other delivery methods — The `retryCount > 1` branch can delete non-SMS `WorkflowReminder` records regardless of their scheduled date. Move `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` outside `OR` so it applies to both the date and retry-count predicates.

Retry bookkeeping failures abort the remaining SMS reminder batch — If `prisma.workflowReminder.update` fails inside the catch, its exception escapes and skips all remaining reminders. Wrap the retry update in a separate try/catch and log failures so processing continues.

goldensDetail.text: retryCount is set to reminder.retryCount + 1 from a value read at the start of the run instead of an atomic increment, so overlapping runs can lose increments.
The deleteMany OR clause applies retryCount > 1 without the SMS method filter, so the SMS cron deletes any workflow reminder (email, WhatsApp) with retryCount above 1.

The retry-count update inside the catch block is not guarded, so if it throws (for example the reminder was deleted concurrently) the error escapes the loop and the cron run fails, skipping the remaining reminders.
Claims transient errors increment retryCount, so two runs during an outage delete the whole pending SMS reminder queue.

SMS-sending locks are counted as failed scheduling attempts: scheduleSMS returns undefined for locked users/teams, retryCount is incremented, and after two cron runs the retryCount > 1 cleanup deletes future reminders even if sending is later unlocked.

findings.description: Backup-code login bypasses password verification when a TOTP code is supplied — A valid `backupCode` plus any nonempty `totpCode` can authenticate without a password because the password guard skips verification and the backup-code branch never validates TOTP. Require password verification for password-based backup-code login even when `totpCode` is supplied.

Concurrent logins can reuse or restore single-use backup codes — Concurrent requests can read the same `backupCodes` state, allowing code reuse or restoring a code consumed by another request. Replace the unconditional `prisma.user.update` with an atomic compare-and-swap against `user.backupCodes`, rejecting or retrying on mismatch, or use a suitably serialized transaction.

Dismissing backup codes leaves 2FA settings stale and modal state unreset — After successful enablement, dismissal through `onOpenChange` skips `onEnable`, leaving the parent's `viewer.me` cache stale and the modal state unreset. Invoke the completion callback and reset modal state on every dismissal after success.

Backup code verification uses timing-dependent secret comparisons — Using `backupCodes.indexOf` makes authentication-secret comparisons timing-dependent and stops at the first match. Validate fixed-format input, compare fixed-length buffers with `crypto.timingSafeEqual`, and scan every slot while retaining the match index; apply the same change in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`.

Backup-code copy test passes without verifying clipboard contents — The test passes even when copying fails or writes incorrect text because `toast-success` appears without awaiting `writeText`. Read the clipboard after clicking `backup-codes-copy` and compare its contents with the displayed backup codes.

Backup-code download test checks the filename but not the contents — An empty or incorrect backup-code file still passes because `download.suggestedFilename()` checks only the filename. Read the downloaded file and compare its contents with the displayed backup codes.

goldensDetail.text: The credentials authorize() skips the password check when any totpCode is present, and the new backup-code branch never validates that totpCode, so a backup code plus a dummy totpCode logs in without the account password.
The getBaseConditions test uses a single booking matching both auth and filter conditions, so it would pass even if the conditions were not combined.
The new public options type makes teamId optional for team scope, so a missing teamId compiles and silently yields empty insights instead of a type error.
Claims getBaseConditions returns OR fragments without parentheses, so a caller appending `AND <extra>` would leak rows outside the authorization scope.

findings.description: Unsanitized feed HTML allows script execution in imported posts — External feed markup can execute scripts on the forum origin because `Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` bypasses sanitization and `absolutize_urls` only rewrites links. Sanitize imported HTML on both creation and update before it reaches `post.cooked`.

Remote article retrieval failures abort Disqus comment imports — A deleted article or unavailable source site makes `TopicEmbed.import_remote` abort the Disqus import before its exported comments are imported. Catch remote retrieval failures and fall back to creating a permalink topic with `PostCreator`.

Conditionless trailing `if` prevents the embed template from compiling — Every embed request that finds an existing topic fails because `end if` generates invalid Ruby in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`. Replace `end if` with `end`.

Feeds without content fields abort polling instead of importing entries — Valid description-only RSS items or summary-only Atom entries leave `i.content` nil, so `scrub` raises and aborts the entire polling run. Fall back to `i.description`, `i.summary`, or an empty string before calling `scrub`.

Missing embed URLs trigger redundant feed refreshes across workers — Concurrent visits or query-string variants trigger repeated synchronous downloads and database work through `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute`, because retrieval throttling is per URL. Coalesce refreshes with a shared feed-level throttle or lock across URLs and workers.

Embedded post dates ignore the user's locale — Month names and date ordering in `post.created_at.strftime("%e %b %Y")` do not follow the user's locale, unlike the surrounding translated labels. Use `I18n.l` with a locale-aware date format.

Concurrent imports of the same URL fail on the unique index — Concurrent imports can both find no embed, causing the second `TopicEmbed.create!` to raise on the unique `embed_url` index instead of returning the existing post. Recover from `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` by fetching the winning embed after rollback, or serialize lookup and creation.

Substring origin check allows unauthorized iframe resize messages — An unrelated window can send accepted resize messages because `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)` accepts partial origin matches. Parse `discourseUrl`, compare its complete origin with `e.origin`, and verify `e.source` matches `iframe.contentWindow`.

Missing-setting tests short-circuit on disabled feed polling — Both tests pass even if their presence checks are removed because `execute` exits while `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is false. Enable polling and provide valid values for every prerequisite except the setting under test, so only that setting prevents `poll_feed`.

Missing-embed_url test fails at the embeddable-host check instead — The assertion passes even without required-parameter validation because `ensure_embeddable` rejects the request before `best` reaches `params.require(:embed_url)`. Configure a valid embeddable host and Referer, omit only `embed_url`, and assert the expected missing-parameter response.

Protocol-relative URLs are incorrectly rewritten to the article host — Protocol-relative `href` and `src` values pass `start_with?('/')` and are rewritten onto the article host, breaking CDN images and changing link destinations. Resolve references against the source URI or handle `//` separately from root-relative paths.

goldensDetail.text: The referer and embed_url host checks compare against SiteSetting.embeddable_host case-sensitively, so a host differing only in case is rejected even though hostnames are case-insensitive.

PollFeed reads i.content.scrub for every feed item, so items without a content element (common in RSS feeds that only have description) raise NoMethodError and abort the import of the remaining items.

TopicEmbed.import appends a footer that interpolates the URL unescaped into an <a href='...'> tag in raw HTML that is later rendered unsanitized, so a crafted URL can inject markup; it also appends to contents with << without handling nil.
When the embedded post has been deleted, TopicEmbed.import's update path passes a nil embed.post to PostRevisor and crashes on every later import of that URL.
Claims import_remote crashes on unparseable pages (nil content) and dead URLs because it does no nil check or network error handling around open(url).read.

absolutize_urls only handles root-relative paths: protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/x.png are rewritten to http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png and path-relative links are left unresolved, breaking links and images in imported posts.

Every retrieval of an article not yet embedded synchronously polls and imports the entire RSS feed, and since throttling is per URL, many different article requests repeat the full feed download and processing.

The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' specs leave feed_polling_enabled at its false default, so they never reach the condition they name and would pass with those checks deleted.
`import_remote` fetches the embed URL with open-uri, which follows redirects, so the embeddable-host check on the initial URL can be bypassed to reach internal services (SSRF).
The retrieve throttle is keyed by the full embed URL, so an anonymous client can vary the query string on the embeddable host to bypass it and make the server create an unbounded number of topics.

The "requires feed_polling_enabled?" spec leaves feed_polling_url and embed_by_username at their blank defaults, so poll_feed is skipped regardless and the test would pass even without the enabled check.
The embed layout references the 'embed' stylesheet and embed.js, but neither is in config.assets.precompile, so with precompiled assets in production the embed page fails to load them.

findings.description: Host validation rejects top-level domains longer than five letters — Administrators cannot configure embedding for legitimate domains such as example.technology because the `host` validator limits top-level domains to five letters. Remove that limit or use validation that accepts current domain names.

Mixed-case URL hostnames fail embeddable host lookup — Case-preserving `uri.host` values cause inconsistent authorization and make `TopicEmbed.import` miss the configured host category. Compare `lower(host)` against `host.downcase` and add mixed-case URL tests.

Empty category query results abort the embeddable hosts migration — An empty `embed_category` query result makes `[0]['id']` raise before the `category_id` fallback runs, aborting migration even on sites without embedding. Check for a result row before extracting its ID, and handle empty results in the fallback query too.

Migrated scheme-prefixed hosts no longer match embedding requests — Previously allowed scheme-prefixed settings stop authorizing embedding after upgrade because raw SQL bypasses `EmbeddableHost` normalization and `record_for_host` compares against `URI.host`. Normalize each migrated `h` to the model’s hostname representation before inserting it.

Hosts saved with ports never match embedding URLs — Referer authorization and topic retrieval reject valid saved entries such as example.com:8080 because `uri.host` excludes the port. Make `host` normalization and lookup use a consistent hostname/port representation.

Host normalization raises on nil before validation — Missing or null `host` input makes `sub!` raise `NoMethodError` instead of returning the validation error the controller handles. Guard against nil in the normalization callback so invalid input reaches the format validator.

Blank-host expansion test passes without exercising the host guard — Default false values for `embed_truncate` and `has_topic_embed?` make this assertion pass even without the host guard in `expandable_first_post?`. Set both prerequisites true to isolate blank-host behavior, or replace the scenario if that requirement was intentionally removed.

goldensDetail.text: The migration reads execute(...)[0]['id'] for embed_category without checking for an empty result, so installs without that setting stored crash the migration instead of falling back to the uncategorized category.

After saving a host, the component overwrites its category with findById(categoryId); when no category was chosen this is null even though the server saved the uncategorized category, so the row shows no category until reload.
Hosts saved with a port (allowed by the validation regex) are stored as host:port, but lookup compares only URI.host, so those configured hosts never match and embedding fails for them.
EmbeddableHost's host format validation only accepts TLDs of 2-5 letters, so admins cannot add embeddable hosts on longer TLDs like example.technology.

findings.description: Long docked topic titles push header controls beyond the available width — The outer `header-extra-info` flex item retains `min-width: auto`, so the ellipsis rules on `.extra-info-wrapper` cannot constrain long titles within `.contents`. Set `min-width: 0` on the component flex item to let it shrink and keep header controls visible.

goldensDetail.text: The flex-item styles target the inner .extra-info-wrapper instead of the component's root div, so in the flexbox header a long topic title keeps its full width and pushes the navigation panel out instead of being truncated.
The align-items mixin emits no -moz-box-align, so on old Firefox versions using the display:-moz-box fallback the advertised vertical centering is not applied.

Removing the float-based right alignment of .d-header .panel leaves the server-rendered (no-JS) header's login panel, which sits inside .row and is not a flex item, no longer right-aligned next to the title.

Making .small-action a flex container leaves .small-action-desc content-sized (no flex:1), so the right-floated edit/delete buttons inside it sit right after short action descriptions instead of at the right edge of the row.

On mobile the .small-action custom message keeps margin-left:-40px, tuned for the old 4em left padding; with the new flex layout and 1.5% padding it is pulled into the avatar column and overlaps the icon.

findings.description: Image upload ceiling incorrectly limits attachment sizes — Attachments allowed by `max_attachment_size_kb` above 10240 are rejected because `maxSizeKB` now caps every upload at 10 MB. Apply the ceiling only to images and retain the configured attachment limit.

Duplicate downsize definition breaks width-and-height calls — Existing width-and-height calls to `downsize` fail because Ruby replaces the earlier definition, causing `optimize` to receive numeric `opts` or raising an argument-count error. Preserve the API with one argument-normalizing `self.downsize` method, or rename the dimensions-based helper.

HTTP 413 upload errors report an unknown server limit as 10 MB — Users receiving HTTP `413` may be told their rejected upload is below the stated maximum because `maxSizeKB` does not reflect the web server’s limit. Use the effective server limit or translated wording without a numeric maximum.

goldensDetail.text: downsize is defined twice in OptimizedImage; the new (from, to, dimensions, opts) version overrides the (max_width, max_height) one, so existing callers such as ResizeEmoji that pass width and height now raise ArgumentError.

The client-side upload size check hardcodes 10 MB instead of the per-type max_<type>_size_kb setting, so attachment limits diverge from the server: larger allowed attachments are blocked and smaller limits are only enforced server-side.
The upload downsizing passes a percentage ('80%') as dimensions, but for animated GIFs the gifsicle path uses --resize-fit, which expects WxH geometry, so downsizing silently fails.
Auto-downsizing passes the upload tempfile path, which lacks a .gif extension, so the animated branch is never chosen and convert keeps only the first frame, flattening oversized animated GIFs.
Claims the downsize loop checking tempfile.size may never terminate because of a stale cached size, causing infinite loops.
Oversized SVG uploads go through the new ImageMagick downsize loop because SVG counts as an image, so the vector file is rasterized or corrupted in place before Upload.create_for parses it as SVG.

The upload tempfile path, which for API URL uploads embeds the request-controlled type param, is now passed to OptimizedImage.downsize and run unescaped in a shell via backticks, allowing command injection through type.
The 413 upload error message states a hard-coded 10 MB maximum that may not match the limit the server or web server actually enforces.

findings.description:
Unconditional pagination hides public group members beyond the first 50 — Public users cannot reach later members because the public group-members route calls `findMembers` once and its template only renders `members`. Add pagination or load-more support to that consumer, or preserve the endpoint’s unpaginated default.

**Also found in:**
- `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6:10-11`
- `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6:8-11`

Removing a member leaves a stale primary-group reference — The replaced update path cleared `User.primary_group_id` through `Group#destroy_deletions`, but `GroupUser` has no equivalent callback. Clear the matching primary-group reference in the same transaction as `group.users.delete(user_id)`.

Stale member responses overwrite the latest navigation — Rapid Next/Previous navigation can display the wrong page when an older response overwrites `offset` and `members` after the latest response arrives. Guard response application in `findMembers` with a request generation token.

Stale member counts leave pagination on an empty page after removal — Removing the sole member at `offset` 50 leaves administrators viewing an empty page despite 50 remaining members because `findMembers` uses stale `user_count`. Refresh the total before clamping `offset` to the start of the last valid page.

Exact multiples of the page size produce an extra empty page — `showingLast` leaves Next enabled on the actual last page when the member count is an exact multiple of the page size. Calculate `totalPages` with `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` while preserving the zero-member behavior.

goldensDetail.text: The admin group pager computes total pages as floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so when the member count is an exact multiple of the limit it shows an extra page and Next navigates to an empty member list.
Paging actions fire overlapping member requests and each response unconditionally overwrites offset and members, so a stale response arriving last can revert the list to an earlier page.
The public members endpoint now always caps results at 50 per page, but the public group members page has no pagination, so groups with more than 50 members are silently truncated for users.
Creating a group ignores the alias_level the admin selected, saving only name and visibility, so new groups keep the default alias level.
Removing a member deletes the membership row directly and skips clearing the user's primary_group_id, so a removed user can keep this group as their primary group.
Group member pagination is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit: Next moves to offset == user_count and shows an empty page.
Admin remove_member deletes memberships with group.users.delete, which skips GroupUser callbacks, so the cached groups.user_count is never decremented and stays inflated.

Admin add_members pushes every username into group.users without skipping existing members, so adding someone already in the group hits the unique group_users index, returns a 500 and leaves earlier users partially added.
The public group members endpoint takes `limit` from params with no upper bound or positivity check, letting a visitor request huge pages or trigger a 500 with a negative limit.
Admin remove_member calls group.users.delete with a raw integer id, which raises RecordNotFound (404/500) when the user is not or no longer a member, e.g. on concurrent removal.

findings.description: Fallback translations are not loaded outside controller requests — Background jobs and mailers calling `I18n.t` can miss available English translations because `translate` loads only the active locale and implicit backend loading is disabled. Load the complete fallback chain at the translation boundary rather than relying on the controller filter to call `ensure_loaded!`.

Translation cache ignores site-specific fallback locale — Sites with different `SiteSetting.default_locale` values can receive incorrect cached translations because the accelerator cache key omits that fallback context. Include the site fallback locale in the cache key or invalidate cached translations whenever it changes.

goldensDetail.text: Fallback locale catalogs are only loaded in the controller's set_locale filter, while translate loads just the current locale, so translations outside requests (jobs, mailers) cannot fall back to the site default or English.

The translation cache key does not include the site or its default locale, but fallback results now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, so multisite processes or a changed default locale serve stale fallback translations.

findings.description: Missing device IDs bypass the anonymous device limit — `Authenticate` grants anonymous access when `TagDevice` returns nil for an empty `X-Grafana-Device-Id`; check `TagDevice` in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go`. Require a device identifier or establish a server-controlled identifier before granting anonymous access when the limit is enabled.

Failed device registration stays cached and bypasses the limit on retry — A device rejected with `ErrDeviceLimitReached` can authenticate on retry because `tagDeviceUI` populates `localCache` before the store write, causing subsequent requests to skip admission checks. Cache only successful registrations or remove the entry on failure.

**Also found in:**
- `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44-46`

Concurrent device admissions can exceed the configured limit — Distinct devices can both pass `CountDevices` before either is inserted, allowing admissions beyond `deviceLimit`. Serialize the count-and-admission operation at the database level across server instances.

goldensDetail.text: tagDeviceUI caches the device key before CreateOrUpdateDevice; when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the entry stays, so the next request from the same device skips the limit check and authenticates for up to 29 minutes.
The new auth.anonymous device_limit setting has no entry in conf/defaults.ini, so the GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT environment override is ignored and the limit stays 0.

findings.description: Background replication can reorder mutations and resurrect deleted objects — A delayed `Legacy.Create` can run after `Legacy.Delete` and resurrect an object, while concurrent updates can leave stale data. Serialize replication per object, including `DeleteCollection` interactions, or use version-aware, durably ordered replication.

Request cancellation aborts asynchronous legacy writes — The request's `ctx` is canceled when the HTTP handler finishes, so legacy writes can fail immediately instead of receiving their intended 10-second window. Apply `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` before `context.WithTimeoutCause` in all four asynchronous write paths to preserve request values without inheriting cancellation.

Legacy updates recompute mutations instead of replicating committed state — Reevaluating `objInfo` against different backend states can produce different objects, especially for patches. Pass the committed `Storage.Update` result, `res`, to `Legacy.Update` through `updateWrapper` rather than independently recomputing the mutation.

Successful deletes use object names instead of kinds in metric labels — Passing `name` to `recordStorageDuration` splits successes and failures across incompatible labels and can create a separate time series for every deleted object. Pass `options.Kind` instead, matching the failure path and other operations.

Storage create and update failures are counted as legacy operations — Using `recordLegacyDuration` hides storage errors from storage metrics and counts legacy operations that never occurred. Use `recordStorageDuration` on both the `Storage.Create` and `Storage.Update` failure paths.

**Also found in:**
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:129-129`

Legacy collection deletion is recorded in unified-storage metrics — Using `recordStorageDuration` for `Legacy.DeleteCollection` double-counts storage operations and leaves legacy collection failures absent from legacy metrics. Record this call with `recordLegacyDuration` instead.

Mode-3 write tests do not verify legacy backend writes — These tests would pass even if asynchronous `Legacy.Update` were removed; `Create`, `Delete`, and `DeleteCollection` have the same coverage gap. Use separate backend mocks, wait for legacy calls to complete, and assert their arguments and invocation counts.

**Also found in:**
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:219-230`

goldensDetail.text: The legacy DeleteCollection goroutine records its duration with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, misattributing legacy latency and errors to the storage metric.
Delete's success path records the storage metric with the object name in the kind label instead of options.Kind, creating per-object series and inconsistent labels.
On storage Create/Update failure the duration is recorded with recordLegacyDuration, attributing unified-store errors to the legacy metric.

Mode 3 legacy writes now run in background goroutines derived from the request context, which is cancelled when the request completes, so legacy writes can be cancelled and legacy storage falls out of sync.
Legacy.Update now receives the original objInfo instead of a wrapper carrying the object stored in unified storage, so legacy recomputes the update and can diverge.
The Mode 3 tests never wait for or assert the asynchronous legacy writes, and legacy and storage share one mock, so removing the legacy calls would not fail them.
Independent per-request goroutines remove ordering between legacy writes to the same resource, so legacy can end up with an older version or a resurrected object.
Mode 3 legacy-storage write errors (create/update/delete/delete-collection) are no longer logged after moving to async goroutines; only a duration metric with an error flag is recorded.
DualWriterMode3.Delete now returns on any unified-storage error, including NotFound, before deleting from legacy, so objects that exist only in legacy can no longer be deleted.

findings.description: Concurrent index builds can overwrite instances and lose event updates — Concurrent calls to `getOrCreateIndex` can build separate instances for one missing key, and the last cache publication can discard event updates applied to the other instance. Serialize construction per key and recheck the cache under that coordination, while allowing different keys to build concurrently.

Initialization document count can race with cache writes — During initialization, `TotalDocs()` iterates `bleveBackend.cache` while the event consumer can add entries, risking a concurrent map iteration/write crash; check `pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go`. Protect the iteration with `cacheMu.RLock` or iterate a snapshot taken under that lock.

goldensDetail.text: BuildIndex now locks only the final cache assignment, so concurrent callers for the same uncached key all build the same expensive index in parallel and the last one overwrites the others.

The new startup log calls TotalDocs, which iterates the index cache without a lock, after the event goroutine that can add indexes has started, so a concurrent map read and write can crash the process.
The PR skips the storage-server module integration test on postgres instead of fixing the failure, removing coverage of the new eager initialization on postgres.

findings.description: Silence notifications action does nothing for Prometheus-only Grafana rules — Clicking the action opens no drawer because `RuleActionsButtons.V2` mounts `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` succeeds, but `rule` is now undefined. Support Prometheus-only rules in the drawer path or load the required ruler DTO when invoked.

Prom-only rule actions omit Pause and Delete — Authorized users lose actions because `AlertRuleMenu` still requires `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` for Pause and `rulerRule` for Delete, but this caller supplies only `promRule`. Migrate the menu and handlers to support Prometheus-only rules, or retain the ruler input until they do.

Combined-rule abilities no longer enforce federated-group immutability — Consumers of `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` now receive update/delete support for federated Mimir rules because `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` hardcodes `isFederated` to false. Preserve group-level federation information when delegating, or retain the `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` guard in the wrapper.

Skipped Grafana rule checks can grant datasource rule abilities — `AlertRuleMenu` combines these results with ruler abilities, so Grafana create permission can expose Duplicate for datasource rules even when datasource abilities deny it. Return neutral abilities for `skipToken` instead of using `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined)`, which enables `duplicateSupported` after loading.

goldensDetail.text: The pause menu item is still gated on a Grafana ruler rule, but the list view now passes only the Prometheus rule, so Pause/Resume disappears for list-view rules even when the user may pause them.
The Delete menu item still requires a ruler rule, which list-view Grafana rules no longer provide, so users with delete permission lose the Delete action.

When the Grafana prom-rule branch is skipped (datasource rules), useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) still reports Duplicate as supported and allowed by Grafana create permission, and AlertRuleMenu ORs it with the ruler ability, so Duplicate appears on cloud rules even when the ruler check denies it.

For list-view Grafana rules RuleActionsButtons gets only promRule, so the Silence menu item is shown but the silence drawer, still gated on a ruler alerting rule, never renders and clicking Silence does nothing.

findings.description: Lazy grant registration allows shortcut collisions to corrupt token context — A newly deployed grant can overwrite `grantsByShortcuts` while `grantsToShortcuts` retains the old mapping, causing previously issued tokens to decode with the wrong grant context. Reject shortcut collisions during lazy registration and keep both mappings consistent under concurrent registration.

Unknown-grant test accepts unrelated runtime failures — Catching `RuntimeException` lets unrelated failures, including `NullPointerException` during factory lookup, pass as successful validation. Assert `IllegalArgumentException` for the unrecognized `ac` shortcut, preferably checking the unknown-grant diagnostic.

Access token ID matcher accepts incorrect grant metadata — Incorrect grant metadata passes because `substring(3, 5)` checks the wrong characters and the equality test rejects matches. Require `items[0]` to have six characters and reject it when `substring(4, 6)` differs from `expectedGrantShortcut`.

Grant shortcut documentation suggests an unsupported three-character length — Custom grants following this documentation can produce token IDs that `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` rejects because its six-character context reserves only two characters for the grant. Document that `getShortcut()` must return exactly two characters, unique across grants.

**Also found in:**
- `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:74-76`

Null rawTokenId bypasses constructor validation — A null `rawTokenId` becomes literal text in `encodeTokenId`, so decoding returns a different, non-null ID and breaks round-tripping. Pass `rawTokenId` to `Objects.requireNonNull` instead of checking `grantType` again.

Concurrent group-read failures can escape the exception assertion — An in-flight read can append to `caughtExceptions` after the assertion passes, or the reader may never run before deletion finishes. Retain the reader thread, coordinate startup with a latch, and join it after setting `deletedAll` before asserting that `caughtExceptions` is empty.

Choice expressions bypass HTML and anchor validation — Translations in `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit.seconds` can introduce malicious links when evaluated by `LinkExpirationFormatterMethod`. Change `value.replaceAll` to normalize only choice comparison operators, preserving every branch’s text for HTML and anchor validation.

Overlapping prefix and suffix scans crash verification of malformed HTML — Malformed HTML such as an unclosed paragraph can make `value.substring` throw `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` instead of reporting illegal HTML. Bound the suffix scan by both string lengths minus `start` so `end` cannot overlap the matched prefix.

Lithuanian OTP setup instructions are in Italian — Users selecting Lithuanian receive `loginTotpStep1` in Italian. Translate it into Lithuanian and update the identical `totpStep1` replacement in `theme/base/account/messages/messages_lt.properties`.

goldensDetail.text: The diff-trimming code computes common prefix and suffix independently, so they can overlap and substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the verifier instead of reporting the illegal HTML.

The account and admin UI bundles now use Java MessageFormat placeholders and choice syntax for error-invalid-multivalued-size, but i18next expects {{n}}, so the UI shows literal {0}/{1}/{2} and the raw choice text.

findings.description: Global MANAGE grants do not imply VIEW for client listing — Permission-only managers receive HTTP 403 from inherited `canList()` and cannot list client scopes because `canView()` ignores global `MANAGE` grants. Make global `MANAGE` imply `VIEW` while preserving resource-specific denial checks.

Global VIEW grant bypasses client-specific VIEW denial — Calling `canView()` here skips individual policy evaluation, violating the grant/denial semantics tested by `testViewUserPermission`. Use `canViewClientDefault()` for the administrative-role bypass and retain `hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)` for resource evaluation with the all-clients fallback.

**Also found in:**
- `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:86-87`

Negative scope-removal test can pass on an unrelated view denial — The test can pass even if unauthorized removal succeeds because `getDefaultClientScopes()` can throw the expected `ForbiddenException` first. Fetch the scope ID through the privileged realm client outside the try block, then assert `ForbiddenException` only around the unprivileged `removeDefaultClientScope()` call.

goldensDetail.text: Claims the removal-cleanup listener is guarded by the V1 fine-grained flag, so client/role/group permissions are orphaned when V1 is disabled or only V2 is enabled.

getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 only finds the type-level 'Clients' resource and returns its name, never actual client ids, so callers that resolve the returned values as client ids get wrong results or null clients.
