Claims getResourceTypeResource can return null in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, causing a NullPointerException in findByResource.
ClientPermissionsV2.canView() ignores a global MANAGE permission, so admins with only global manage take the unpaginated, per-client evaluated listing path.
canView(client) short-circuits on the global all-clients VIEW permission, so a client-specific permission denying an admin is never evaluated and the client is still viewable.

The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, an admin granted a permission on all clients is denied on any client that also has its own per-client permission resource, because only the per-client resource is evaluated.

ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AbstractTokenExchangeProvider still calls clients().canExchangeTo for client-to-client exchange, so with token exchange and FGAP V2 enabled the request fails with a server error instead of a permission decision.

findings.description: Passkey-only users reach an unusable password form with the legacy theme — The legacy `keycloak` theme inherits `login-password.ftl`, which lacks `passkeys.conditionalUIData`, so passkey-only users cannot authenticate after `DefaultAuthenticationFlow` skips credential setup. Add the passkey macro to the base `login-password.ftl` as well as the `keycloak.v2` override.

Organization-aware eligibility skips required login cache invalidation — A disabled organization can leave a hidden or link-only IDP cached, exposing it after re-enabling because the login bean checks only `isEnabled`. Reload `original` through `idpDelegate.getById` before applying `getLoginPredicate()` so both models use database-level eligibility.

Login-query cache test never verifies a cache hit — An implementation of `getForLogin` that always queries the delegate while populating the cache would still pass this test. Repeat lookups before invalidation, including one for the same organization, and assert that they do not invoke the delegate or otherwise demonstrate an observable cache hit.

goldensDetail.text: The test registers cleanup for the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases, so the created identity providers are never cleaned up.

Adding the organization/BROKER_PUBLIC check to the shared LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate also changes IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate, so with organizations disabled a user's linked IdP that has an organizationId but is not public is no longer shown on the login page.

findings.description: Feature-enabled table widgets discard fetched data and render empty — Organizations with `use-table-widget-visualization` see empty table widgets even when queries return data. Populate `columns` and `tableData` with the fetched columns, rows, and metadata instead of placeholders.

Hidden attributes remain visible when the search query is empty — The default drawer still displays `is_segment`, `project_id`, and `received` because the empty-search path returns `sorted` before filtering. Apply `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` filtering before that early return.

Rejected browser reports expose sensitive payloads in warning logs — Logging `raw_report` copies arbitrary report bodies and document URLs into warning logs, potentially exposing personal information or tokens even when info logging is suppressed. Restrict `logger.warning` metadata to validation field names, error codes, and non-sensitive report metadata.

Attribute key cache is shared across organizations — Switching organizations with identical selections can display cached attribute names from the previous organization because `useGetTraceItemAttributeKeys` fetches organization-specific data. Include the organization slug or ID in `queryKey` and its memoization dependencies.

Zero values bypass mutual exclusion of age and timestamp — Reports containing both `age: 0` and `timestamp: 0` pass validation despite the fields being mutually exclusive. Check membership in `initial_data` instead of truthiness in both validators.

Custom cell renderers discard valid falsy ReactNode results — Callers cannot intentionally hide cells with `null` or render custom zeros because `if (cell)` substitutes the original content for valid falsy results. Check `cell !== undefined` and use the equivalent explicit check for the header renderer.

goldensDetail.text: The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators check truthiness via initial_data.get(), so a zero value is treated as absent and a report carrying both fields passes validation.
The validation-failure warning logs the entire raw, attacker-controlled browser report instead of a redacted subset.
The Snuba replay lookup for error IDs runs even when enable_error_context=false, adding a needless query (and failure point) to opt-out requests.

With the use-table-widget-visualization flag on, the widget renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded empty columns and data instead of the query results, so every table widget shows an empty table.
The custom cell renderers fall back to default rendering on any falsy return (0, '', null), not only undefined, so a renderer cannot render zero or an empty cell.
The attribute-keys query key no longer includes the organization slug, so two organizations with the same filters share a cache entry and switching orgs can show the previous org's attribute names.

Every paginated breadcrumb-summary request queries the replay and fetches all of its error events from nodestore with no cap, adding latency and memory proportional to the replay's error count on each page.
HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES is applied only when a search query is present; the no-search early return shows all attributes, so the hidden attributes still appear in the default span attributes view.

The bulk delete test sets max_segment_id to None to cover the new guard in _make_recording_filenames, but it mocks delete_matched_rows, so the guard is never executed and removing it would not fail the test.
Error event timestamps (seconds) are compared with replay recording event timestamps (milliseconds), so errors are not interleaved chronologically with breadcrumbs.

findings.description: Memory backpressure repeats cluster-wide Redis queries for each flusher — With memory backpressure enabled, each buffer's `get_memory_info()` calls `iter_cluster_memory_usage` for the entire cluster, multiplying Redis INFO requests regardless of assigned shards. Query cluster memory once per submission instead of once per buffer.

Zero process limit unexpectedly starts one worker per assigned shard — Passing `--flusher-processes 0` can unexpectedly spawn many workers because `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats zero as missing. Default only when `max_processes is None` and reject explicitly supplied limits that are not positive.

Patched-out sleep allows shutdown to race with span flushing — Shutdown can stop the background flusher before spans are flushed because this test patches `time.sleep` to return immediately, and `join()` sets the stopped flag before waiting. Wait for observable flush output with a real timeout before initiating shutdown.

Hung spawn workers are not killed before replacement — A replacement can run alongside the original on the same shards because spawn workers are `SpawnProcess` instances, so the `multiprocessing.Process` guard skips `kill()`. Check against `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` so the old worker is killed before replacement.

Expired shutdown deadline skips termination of remaining workers — Workers left running after shutdown can overlap with new shard owners during a rebalance because `break` skips cleanup once `remaining_time` expires. Apply the deadline only to waiting and still terminate every remaining process.

goldensDetail.text: The restart path only kills a hung flusher if it is a multiprocessing.Process, but spawn-context workers are SpawnProcess, so hung processes are never killed and a duplicate flusher is started for the same shards.
join() breaks out of the per-process loop when the shared deadline expires, skipping termination of the remaining flusher processes and leaving them running after shutdown.

findings.description: Empty-array test passes a dictionary instead of an array — Broken array handling in `AssignmentSource.from_dict` goes undetected because `test_from_dict_empty_array` supplies a dictionary. Rename this case to `test_from_dict_empty_dict` and add a separate `test_from_dict_empty_array` case passing `[]`.

Default queued timestamp is fixed at module import time — Every `AssignmentSource` created without an explicit `queued` value receives the module-import timestamp, making the value serialized by `to_dict` stale. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each instance records its own creation time.

Predictable OAuth state allows GitHub account substitution — An attacker can link their GitHub account to another user's active pipeline because `pipeline.signature` hashes view class names rather than identifying an authorization attempt. Generate a cryptographically random state, store it in the session-bound pipeline, and validate and consume it on callback.

Missing integration records bypass installer ownership verification — An authenticated GitHub user can bypass installer ownership verification when the webhook has not yet created the `Integration` record. Verify ownership in the `Integration.DoesNotExist` path too, or fail and retry once the record exists instead of calling `pipeline.next_step()`.

**Also found in:**
- `src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:500-505`

Optional sender metadata causes installation reattachment to fail — Reattaching an active, unlinked integration without optional sender metadata raises an unhandled `KeyError` and returns a 500; check the integration builder's conditional sender population. Validate `integration.metadata`, `sender`, and `login`, returning the invalid-installation response when they are unavailable.

Runtime translation lookup hides payload error messages from extraction — Django's translation extractor cannot collect payload messages passed through `_(error_short)` because it requires marked literals. Wrap the default and each caller's literal in `_()` and put the translated value directly in the payload.

Missing-installation test passes on an unrelated OAuth state failure — This test can pass without exercising installation lookup because `OAuthLoginView` returns the same error for invalid state. Complete OAuth with valid pipeline state and verify that the installation lookup returns 404 before asserting the error response.

goldensDetail.text: test_installation_not_found uses a wrong OAuth state, so it fails at the state check and never reaches the installation-not-found path it is meant to test.

findings.description: Metric alert handler cannot be instantiated after switching to abstract base — Instantiating `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now raises `TypeError` because `StatefulDetectorHandler` requires `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Implement those methods or retain the concrete `DetectorHandler` base until the stateful implementation is ready.

Occurrence assertions ignore the measurement passed to the builder — Passing a constant or another group's measurement to `build_occurrence_and_event_data` still passes these tests because `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` ignores `value`. Include `value` in the mock occurrence and use actual packet values in expectations, or assert the builder's call arguments.

goldensDetail.text: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing its abstract methods, so instantiating it for metric alert detectors raises TypeError where it previously returned an empty-result handler.

The mock occurrence builder ignores its value argument, so tests (e.g. group_2 expected with 6 while the packet carries 10) pass regardless of which value is passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data.
